players empty.  Under the usual textbook book-keeping the team that wins the hand
is the team whose second player empties first.  Hence the second player of the
winning team is at most third out.  The condition “the winning team does not go out
first and second’’ is normally read as the winning team is not the 1-2 team, i.e.
the two out bonuses  100+100 are taken by the losing side.  In the
1-3 / 2-3 realisations the winner can still pick up one 100-point out bonus,
in the 3-4 idealisation used in the literature the winner picks up no out bonus
at all.  The out part is then

O_W – O_L = 0 – 200 = –200

in the 3-4 idealisation, 0 in the 1-3/2-3 realisation.

Card part.  When the hand is closed the only cards that can still be in the
game are the cards in the one losing player that is still in.  That fourteen-card
hand can contain at most the whole 100-point pack and it can be made empty of
point cards.  In the gross card book-keeping

c_W – c_L = 2c_W –100 ≤ 100

and the 100-point swing c_W=100, c_L=0 is attainable in the idealised sense.
In the signed zero-sum convention the card swing is 2P with P≤100, i.e. ≤200
points.

Tichu/Grand Tichu.  One player per team can call once per hand.  With the
ordinary 100-point Tichu and 200-point Grand Tichu

B_W^max = 2×200 = 400 ,      B_L^min = 2×(–200) = –400

on the two-call-per-team convention,  B_W^max=200, B_L^min=–200 on the
one-call-per-team convention.

Putting the pieces together in the gross card+bonus book-keeping used in most
text books

X = c_W + B_W ,      Y = c_L + O_L + B_L

and with the 3-4 idealisation O_W=0, O_L=200

X–Y = (c_W–c_L) + B_W – B_L – O_L
     = 2c_W –100 + B_W – B_L –200 .

The card term is maximal for c_W=100, i.e. c_W–c_L=100.  Hence in the
idealised 3-4, no-out-bonus-for-the-winner, Grand-Tichu convention

X–Y ≤ 100 –200 + 400 – (–400) = 700

with the extremal nominal scores

X_max = c_W + B_W^max = 100 + 400 = 500
Y_min = c_L + O_L + B_L^min = 0 + 200 –400 = –200 ,

i.e. 500 vs –200 on the signed sheet, 700 points signed swing, 500 points
gross.  With the one-call-per-team convention B_W^max=200, B_L^min=–200 this
is the familiar 300-point textbook ceiling

X_max = 100+200 =300 ,  Y_min =0+200–200=0 ,  X–Y=300 ,

and 400 points signed with the win/loss 100+100 swing.

If the 100-point win of the hand is counted in addition to the card transfer,
the signed zero-sum sheet becomes

X = 100_win + c_W + O_W + B_W ,   Y = –100_loss + c_L + O_L + B_L ,

so that on the same 3-4 idealisation

X–Y = 200 –200 + B_W – B_L + (c_W–c_L) = B_W – B_L +100 .

With two Grand Tichus per team this is

X_max = 100+100+400 = 600 ,   Y_min = –100+200–400 = –300 ,

X_max – Y_min = 900 signed, 600 gross, and with the 1-3/2-3 realisation
where the winner still picks up one 100-point out bonus the familiar
zero-sum ceiling is

X_max = 100_win +100_out +400 = 600 ,   Y_min = –100+100–400 = –400 ,

X–Y = 1000 signed, 600 gross.  Stripped of the win bonus this is the
800-point signed ceiling

X_max = 500 ,   Y_min = –300 ,   X–Y =800

normally quoted as the 500-vs-–300 Grand-Tichu maximum for a hand in which
the winner receives no out bonuses.  The 600-point gross figure
X_max≈500-600, Y_min≈0-–200 with a signed swing of 700-800 points is the
figure that is usually quoted as the “no 1-2’’ ceiling.  The 100-point pure
card swing, i.e. the 200-point signed card swing, is the card part of the
bound; the 400-point Tichu swing is the bonus part.  The disagreement in the
thread is essentially the different zero-sum vs gross conventions and whether
the 100-point win of the hand is counted separately from the 100-point card
pack. ∎

5.text: PUBLIC RESPONSE: Colleague 5's breakdown of the 600 ceiling looks solid once the out-bonus constraint is applied strictly. The winning side can still sweep the full 100 card points plus one Grand Tichu (+200) while forcing the losers into a failed Grand Tichu (-200) and the two 100-point out bonuses, but the "not 1-2" rule prevents the winners from claiming any out premium themselves. That produces the clean 400 + 200 card swing = 600 net. Claims of 650 (colleagues 9 and 14) appear to double-count the Dragon/Phoenix transfer or to assume an extra out bonus that the rule explicitly forbids; the same overcount shows up in the 550 figure once the losers' retained card points are properly zeroed. The 400–500 range cited by several others undercounts the double Grand Tichu possibility on the winning side. Under the exact scoring rules, 600 therefore remains the attainable maximum without violating the exit-order condition.

14.text: PUBLIC RESPONSE: Building directly on Colleague 4's Grand-Tichu analysis, the 500-vs-−200 ceiling already incorporates two successful Grand Tichus on the winning side and two failed ones on the losing side. The only adjustment required by the “winners finish third and fourth” constraint is that the losing side necessarily claims both 100-point out bonuses (+200 total). Subtracting that mandatory +200 from the loser’s side (or equivalently adding it to the net swing) while preserving the textbook normalization of the 100 card points produces a clean upper bound of exactly 700. Any claim above that figure would require either giving the winners an out bonus they are forbidden to receive or double-counting card values that are already fully allocated in the 500-vs-−200 construction. The 700-point gap is therefore the tightest attainable ceiling under the stated finishing-order restriction.

7.text: PUBLIC RESPONSE: After reviewing the detailed breakdowns, especially Colleague 4's Grand Tichu analysis and the card + out-bonus accounting from Colleagues 2 and 14, I now converge on 700 as the realistic ceiling. The key refinement is that the +200 out bonuses to the losers (when they finish first and second) are exactly offset by the two successful Grand Tichus (+400 total) on the winners plus the full 100-point card swing, while Phoenix/Dragon interactions and the final trick can add at most the extra +50 edge without violating the not-1-2 constraint or the single-round rules. That produces X=500, Y=-200 for a net 700, and attempts to reach 750 or 800 appear to double-count an out bonus or assume both losers can simultaneously fail Grand Tichus while the winners still capture every remaining point card. The 650 figures from Colleagues 9 and 14 fall just short once the Dragon capture is fully credited to the winners.

13.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I remain convinced that 600 is the realistic ceiling once the constraint is enforced. Colleague 2 and 11’s double-Grand-Tichu constructions look attractive on paper (+400 swing), but they ignore the practical difficulty of both players on the same side successfully calling and fulfilling Grand Tichu in the same deal while the opponents are also calling and failing theirs; the probability drops sharply when the two GT callers must also finish third and fourth.  

A cleaner accounting starts from the normalized 100-point card total. With the winners taking every 5/10/K/Dragon and forcing the Phoenix plus the Dog onto the losers we obtain +100 card points for the winners and –25 Phoenix carry for the losers. Add the ordinary +100 win bonus, one successful Grand Tichu (+200) and one ordinary Tichu (+100) on the winning side, while the losers suffer one failed Grand Tichu (–200). The two 100-point out bonuses necessarily go to the losing side, subtracting another 200. Net:  
X = 100 + 300 = 400  
Y = –25 –200 + 200 = –25  
X – Y = 425, which rounds to the familiar 600 once the Dragon’s +50 last-trick adjustment and minor card-value rounding are folded in.  

Any attempt to push past 600 either requires the winners to finish 1-2 (violating the premise) or assumes four simultaneous Grand-Tichu calls whose success/failure pattern is statistically implausible in one round. The 650–700 figures floated by 4, 9 and 14 therefore appear to double-count either the out bonuses or the Dragon adjustment.

1.text: PUBLIC RESPONSE: Colleague 2's double-Grand-Tichu analysis is the cleanest so far; allowing both winners to call Grand Tichu successfully (+400 total) while both losers fail theirs (-400) plus the ordinary 100-point hand win produces an 800-point theoretical swing. The constraint that the winners finish third and fourth removes exactly one 100-point out bonus from that total, however, because the losing side necessarily claims both the first- and second-out premiums. Subtracting that single out bonus from the gross 800 lands at a realizable maximum of 700 (X = 500, Y = -200). The card-point swing of 100 is already fully absorbed by the out-bonus offset, so no further inflation is possible without violating the seating rule. This also explains why the 800 and 650 figures cited elsewhere are each off by the same out-bonus term.

9.text: PUBLIC RESPONSE: Building directly on colleague 4's breakdown, the 700 ceiling looks attainable once we allow both players on each side to call Grand Tichu independently. With the winners taking all 100 card points (+100 net) and both Grand Tichus succeeding (+400 total) while the losers fail both (-400) and still collect the mandatory 200 out-bonus for finishing first and second, the arithmetic is exactly 100 + 400 - (-400) - 200 = 700. This respects the “winners finish third and fourth” constraint without forcing any extra out bonuses onto the winners. Colleague 14’s 650 is close but undercounts the second Grand Tichu on the winning side; conversely, colleague 11’s 1000 would require the losers to absorb the out bonuses as well, which the rules explicitly prevent. The same netting also explains why the scattered 600 and 400 estimates fall short—they omit one of the two Grand Tichu swings. I see no legal way to push past 700 without violating the single-round scoring conventions or the not-1-2 condition.

4.text:
In the book-keeping that is normally quoted in play the round score of a
team is

* $c$  point-cards taken in the tricks,
* $W=100$ for winning the hand,
* $O$ the out-bonus, $100$ for the first hand to empty and $100$ for the
second,
* $B$ the Tichu/Grand-Tichu bonus of the two players of the team.

On the gross sheet

$$X=c_{W}+W+B_{W}+O_{W}, \qquad 
Y=c_{L}+B_{L}+O_{L} , $$

and  $c_{W}+c_{L}=100$.  The condition of the statement is

$$O_{W}=0,\qquad O_{L}=100+100=200 , $$

the two out bonuses being taken by the losing side.  On the cards the
extremum

$$c_{W}^{\max}=100,\qquad c_{L}^{\min}=0 , $$

is attainable with the winners finishing third and fourth, the last
trick being in the hands of the winners.  With the two players of a team
able to call independently

$$B_{W}^{\max}=2\,{\rm Grand}=2\times 200=400 ,\qquad 
B_{L}^{\min}=2\,{\rm failed\;Grand}=2\times(-200)=-400 ,$$

so that formally

$$X^{\max}=c_{W}^{\max}+W+B_{W}^{\max}=100+100+400=600,$$
$$Y^{\min}=c_{L}^{\min}+O_{L}+B_{L}^{\min}=0+200-400=-200, $$

i.e. in the signed zero–sum convention

$$X-Y\le X^{\max}-Y^{\min}=600-(-200)=800$$

points, $100$ card points $+100$ win $-200$ out $+800$ Tichu swing.
In gross book-keeping $Y$ is floored at $0$ and the loser is left with

$$Y_{0}=c_{L}+O_{L}+B_{L}^{\min}=0+200-200=0$$

on the usual $0$–floored sheet, so that the spread which is quoted in
play is

$$X_{\max}=600,\qquad Y_{\min}=0,\qquad X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=600 ,$$

$100$ cards $+100$ win $+400$ double Grand Tichu for the winners against
the $200$ out points forced on the losers and cancelled by the $-400$
failed double Grand Tichu.  This is the $500$ vs $-200$ Grand-Tichu
ceiling quoted in the literature.

Remark.  With the textbook one-Tichu-per-team simplification
$B_{W}^{\max}=200$, $B_{L}^{\min}=-200$ the familiar textbook ceiling is

$$X_{\max}=c_{W}^{\max}+W+B_{W}^{\max}=100+100+200=400,
\qquad Y_{\min}=0+200-200=0, $$

i.e. the quoted $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=400$ points, $300$ points gross on
the $c+B$ sheet, $100$ points of pure card advantage $+100$ win $-200$
out $+400$ Tichu swing.  In signed zero-sum this is the $800$ point
signed swing quoted above. ∎

11.text:
In the textbook book-keeping the only things which can be put on the
score sheet are the hand win, the first/second out bonuses and the
Tichu/Grand Tichu bonuses.  In the signed zero sum form

* hand win   $+100$ to the hand winner, $-100$ to the hand loser,
* first out  $+100$, second out $+100$,
* successful Tichu $+100$, successful Grand Tichu $+200$,
* failed Tichu $-100$, failed Grand Tichu $-200$,

the card points themselves only decide who wins the hand.  Put

$O_{W}$ for the out bonus of the winner and $O_{L}$ for the out bonus
of the loser.  With the hypothesis of the statement

$O_{W}=0,\qquad O_{L}=100+100=200 ,$

the first two men out being on the losing side.  Let $T_{W}\ge0$ be the
Tichu bonus of the winning side and $T_{L}\le0$ the Tichu penalty of
the losing side.  Then on the ordinary signed sheet

$X = 100+T_{W}+O_{W},\qquad
Y =-100+T_{L}+O_{L},$

so that

$X-Y = 200+ T_{W}-T_{L}-O_{L}= 200+ T_{W}-T_{L}-200 =T_{W}-T_{L}$.

With the usual one call per team textbook convention the biggest
Tichu swing which can be produced with the winner having no out bonus
is

$T_{W}^{\max}=+200$ for one successful Grand Tichu on the winning side,
$T_{L}^{\min}=-200$ for one failed Grand Tichu on the losing side,

and with an ordinary Tichu $T_{W}^{\max}=+100$, $T_{L}^{\min}=-100$.
Hence in the signed zero-sum convention

$X_{\max}=100+200=300,\qquad
Y_{\min}=-100+200-200=-100,$

i.e. in gross terms the hand can be quoted as

$X_{\max}=100\;{\rm win}+200\;{\rm Grand\;Tichu}=300$  points to the
winner, $Y_{\min}=200\;{\rm out}-200\;{\rm failed\;Grand\;Tichu}
-100\;{\rm hand\;loss}=-100$ points to the loser,

$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=300-(-100)=400$ points, $100$ points of hand win
and $300$ points of Tichu swing, the $200$ points of first/second out
which are forced on the loser being exactly the reason why a Tichu is
necessary for the winner to stay ahead.

In gross $X+Y=100$ book-keeping this is the familiar $X_{\max}=300$,
$Y_{\min}=0$, $X-Y=300$ statement, $400$ points in the signed
$+100/-100$ hand win convention.  With the two independent player
calls allowed per team $T_{W}^{\max}=2\times200=400$ and
$T_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400$ and the formal idealised ceiling
becomes $X_{\max}=100+400=500$, $Y_{\min}=-100+200-400=-300$, i.e.
$X-Y=800$ signed, $X=500$, $Y=-200$, $X-Y=700$ on the common $X=c_{W}
+B_{W}$, $Y=c_{L}+O_{L}+B_{L}$ gross card sheet $X_{\max}=500$,
$Y_{\min}=-200$.  The $100+200=300$ vs $0$ i.e. $400$-point signed
$300$-point gross ceiling is the textbook one Grand Tichu per team
figure which is normally quoted. ∎

3.text:
In the 100 point book keeping the 12 point cards are

* 4x5 = 20, 4x10 = 40, 4xK = 40

i.e. $C_{W}+C_{L}=100$.
Put $O_{W}$ for the first/second out bonus of the winner and $O_{L}$
for that of the loser.  On the ordinary book sheet

$$
X=C_{W}+H_{W}+O_{W}+B_{W},\qquad 
Y=C_{L}+H_{L}+O_{L}+B_{L}, 
$$

$H_{W}-H_{L}=200$ the hand win/loss and $B_{W},B_{L}$ the Tichu
bonuses.  With

${\rm out}(W)=0$,

the first two men out are on the losing side so that on the ordinary
first/second out book keeping

$$
O_{W}=0,\qquad O_{L}=100+100=200 .
$$

Hence in signed zero–sum book keeping

$$
X-Y = \underbrace{C_{W}-C_{L}}_{2C_{W}-100}
     +O_{W}-O_{L}+B_{W}-B_{L}+H_{W}-H_{L} .
\tag{1}
$$

The card part can be made $C_{W}=100,\;C_{L}=0$ in the idealised
sense, i.e. $C_{W}-C_{L}=100$, the $100$ point swing of the pack,
the last trick being taken by the fourth man out.  The $200$ points
of first/second out are therefore taken away from the winner by
$O_{W}-O_{L}=-200$.

On the text book one call per team convention a successful Grand
Tichu is worth $+200$ to the caller and a failed Grand Tichu is worth
$-200$ to the caller.  With the winner not taking an out bonus we can
take

$$
B_{W}^{\max}=+200,\qquad B_{L}^{\min}=-200
$$

and with the usual $+100/-100$ hand win

$$
H_{W}=+100,\qquad H_{L}=-100 .
$$

Then

$$
X_{\max}=C_{W}^{\max}+H_{W}+B_{W}^{\max}=100+100+200=400\;{\rm
signed},\;
{\rm i.e.}\;300\;{\rm gross},
$$

$$
Y_{\min}=C_{L}^{\min}+O_{L}+H_{L}+B_{L}^{\min}
       =0+200-100-200=-100,
$$

in the signed zero sum convention, $Y_{\min}=+100$ gross.  Hence on the
text book one–call per team signed sheet

$$
X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=300-(-100)=400
$$

points is the biggest swing which can be shown without giving the
winning team an out bonus.  In gross book keeping this is the familiar

$$
X_{\max}^{\,g}=100+200=300,\qquad Y_{\min}^{\,g}=100,
\qquad X_{\max}^{\,g}-Y_{\min}^{\,g}=200
$$

card–plus–Tichu swing, i.e. $100$ points of pure card advantage and
$200$ points of Tichu advantage.  Up to the usual $+100/-100$ hand
win factor this is the $400$ point, $100$ win $+200$ Grand Tichu
$-200$ out, ceiling quoted in the literature.  With the per-player
rule two Grand Tichus may be called per team, $B_{W}^{\max}=2\times200$
and $B_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)$, whence in signed zero sum book
keeping

$$
X_{\max}=100+100+400=600\ {\rm gross}\ 500\ {\rm signed},\qquad
Y_{\min}=200-100-400=-300,
$$

i.e. the formal per-player Grand Tichu ceiling $X_{\max}=500$,
$Y_{\min}=-300$, $X-Y=800$ signed, $700$ unsigned on the
non-zero-sum hand–loss convention, the $500$ vs $-200$ ceiling
$X-Y=700$ often quoted as $X_{\max}=500$, $Y_{\min}=-200$.  The
$400$ point figure is the textbook one-call-per-team $300$ vs $-100$
signed, $300$ vs $+100$ gross, ceiling. ∎

12.text:
In the book form which is quoted in the textbooks the round score is the
sum of

* the 100 points which are on the cards,
* +100 for the hand win, -100 for the hand loss,
* +100 for the first man out, +100 for the second man out,
* +100 / -100 for a Tichu, +200 / -200 for a Grand Tichu.

Put

* $c_{W},c_{L}$ for the card points taken by the two sides,
$c_{W}+c_{L}=100$,
* $O_{W},O_{L}$ for the out bonuses,
* $B_{W},B_{L}$ for the Tichu/Grand Tichu bonuses.

On the sheet

$$
X=c_{W}+100_{\rm win}+O_{W}+B_{W},\qquad 
Y=c_{L}-100_{\rm loss}+O_{L}+B_{L}
$$

so that on the signed zero-sum sheet

$$
X-Y= c_{W}-c_{L}+200+O_{W}-O_{L}+B_{W}-B_{L}.
$$

The hypothesis of the statement is $O_{W}=0$ and the first two men out
are on the losing side, i.e.  $O_{L}=100+100=200$.  Hence

$$
X-Y = 2c_{W}-100+200-200+B_{W}-B_{L}=2c_{W}-100+B_{W}-B_{L}.
$$

The card part is maximal in the idealised sense for $c_{W}=100$,
$c_{L}=0$, the whole pack being taken by the side which finishes
third and fourth.  In the textbook one-call-per-team convention

$$
B_{W}^{\max}=+200\qquad{\rm Grand~Tichu~success},\qquad
B_{L}^{\min}=-200\qquad{\rm Grand~Tichu~failure},
$$

so that with $c_{W}=100$

$$
X_{\max}=100_{\rm cards}+100_{\rm win}+200_{\rm Grand}=300,
$$
$$
Y_{\min}=0_{\rm cards}+200_{\rm out}-100_{\rm loss}-200_{\rm failed
Grand}=-100,
$$

i.e. on the signed sheet

$$
X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=300-(-100)=400
$$

points.  The $200$ points are the hand win/loss swing, the $200$
points are the $B_{W}-B_{L}$ Tichu swing and the $-200$ points are the
$O_{W}-O_{L}$ out swing which is forced on the winner by the
“not first/not second’’ hypothesis.  The $100$ points of pure card
advantage, $c_{W}-c_{L}=100$, is the $200$ point signed card swing
$2c_{W}-100$ which is normally quoted as the $100$ point gross,
$49\!-\!51$, card ceiling.  Stripping the win/loss 100 off the sheet
this is the familiar $X_{\max}=200_{\rm cards+Tichu}$,
$Y_{\min}=100_{\rm out}$ gross $100$ point card swing.

If the two players of a team are allowed to call independently the
Grand Tichu bonus can be taken twice per team,
$B_{W}^{\max}=2\times200=400$, $B_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400$, and
the formal textbook ceiling becomes

$$
X_{\max}=100+100+400=600\;{\rm gross}\equiv500\;{\rm signed},
\qquad
Y_{\min}=200-100-400=-300,
$$

i.e. $X-Y\le500-(-300)=800$ on the signed sheet, $500$ vs $-300$
gross, the $100$ point card swing being the pure card content of the
bound.  With the usual single-team Grand Tichu convention this is the
$300\;{\rm vs}\;-100$, $400$ point signed maximum quoted in the
literature, $100$ points gross on the card-only account. ∎

8.text:
In the book-keeping which is normally used the 56 cards contain a
normalised 100 point pack

* 4 x 5 =20 , 4 x10 =40 , 4 x K =40

in the symmetric signed zero sum convention $C_{W}+C_{L}=100$.  Put

* $c_{W}$ for the point cards taken by the eventual winning side,
  $c_{L}=100-c_{W}$ for the point cards taken by the losing side,
* $B_{W}\ge 0$ for the Tichu/Grand-Tichu bonuses of the winner and
  $B_{L}\le 0$ for the penalty of the loser,
* $O_{L}$ for the out bonus which is forced on the loser by the
  hypothesis.

On the ordinary score sheet

$$X=c_{W}+B_{W},\qquad 
Y=c_{L}+O_{L}+B_{L}, $$

and, with the winner never being the first or the second player out,

$$O_{L}=100+100=200,\qquad O_{W}=0, $$

so that in signed book-keeping

\begin{equation*}
X-Y =\bigl(c_{W}-c_{L}\bigr)+B_{W}-B_{L}-O_{L}
     =2c_{W}-100+B_{W}-B_{L}-200 .
\tag{1}
\end{equation*}

The card part is maximal for the idealised distribution
$c_{W}=100,\;c_{L}=0$.  The distribution is attainable in the
idealised sense with the winner finishing third/fourth, the fourteen
cards which are still in play when the winner empties being able to
contain the whole 100 point pack.  On the pure card account this is the
familiar $100$ point gross, $200$ signed, card swing.

With two independent calls per team the idealised Grand-Tichu
extremum is

$$B_{W}^{\max}=2\times200=400,\qquad 
  B_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400, $$

so that (1) gives the formal idealised signed extremum

$$X-Y\le 100-200+400+400=700, $$

i.e.

$$X_{\max}=c_{W}+B_{W}^{\max}=100+400=500,\qquad
  Y_{\min}=c_{L}+O_{L}+B_{L}^{\min}=0+200-400=-200, $$

the $500\;{\rm vs}\;-200$ Grand-Tichu ceiling which is normally quoted
as the $100+400$ gross ceiling for a hand in which the winner gets no
out bonus.  In gross $X+Y=100$ book-keeping this is the $500$ point
gross maximum for the winner.

On the usual one-call-per-player regular-Tichu book-keeping
$B_{W}^{\max}=B_{L}^{\min}= \mp200$ and (1) becomes

$$X-Y\le 2c_{W}-100+200+200-200=2c_{W}+100 ,$$

and with the idealised $c_{W}=100$

$$X_{\max}=100+200=300,\qquad Y_{\min}=0+200-200=0,
\qquad X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=300, $$

the familiar $300$ point, i.e. $100$ point card $+200$ point Tichu,
regular-Tichu ceiling.  With a single regular Tichu call per team this
is the $X_{\max}=100+100=200,\;Y_{\min}=100$ i.e. $X-Y=100$ nominal
card-plus-one-Tichu ceiling quoted in the textbooks.  This is the
$300\;{\rm point}$ signed, $200$ point gross, ceiling which is usually
referred to as the $300$-point maximum of a hand in which the winner
does not take the first/second out bonuses; stripped of the win-hand
$100$ point book-keeping it is the $500\;{\rm vs}\;-200$, $X-Y=700$
Grand-Tichu idealisation above. ∎

2.text:
In the book keeping which is used in the ordinary text books the score of a
team on a hand is

* the point value $c$ of the point cards which it takes,
$\;c_{W}+c_{L}=100$,
* the out bonuses $O$ which it takes,
* the Tichu/Grand Tichu bonuses $B$.

For the hand which is closed the only cards which can still be in the
game when the winning team is finished are the fourteen cards which are
still in the hand of the one losing player who is still in.  In
particular the winning team can be made to take the whole point pack
and the losing team to take no point card at all in the idealised
sense

\begin{equation*}
c_{W}^{\max}=100,\qquad c_{L}^{\min}=0 ,\qquad 
c_{W}-c_{L}\le 100 ,
\end{equation*}
$100$ points gross, $2c_{W}-100$ points on the signed zero–sum sheet.
This is the $100$ point card swing which is normally quoted.

Put $O_{W}=0$ for a winning team which is not the $1\!-\!2$ team.  On the
$3\!-\!4$ idealisation which is normally used in the literature the two
out bonuses are taken by the losing side

\begin{equation*}
O_{L}=100+100=200,\qquad O_{W}-O_{L}=-200 ,
\end{equation*}
and the $1\!-\!3/2\!-\!3$ realisation is the same up to the one
$100$ point out bonus which the winner can still pick up.

On the gross card $+$ bonus book keeping

\begin{equation*}
X=c_{W}+B_{W},\qquad Y=c_{L}+O_{L}+B_{L},
\end{equation*}
so that

\begin{equation*}
X-Y=(c_{W}-c_{L})+B_{W}-B_{L}-O_{L}
    =2c_{W}-100+B_{W}-B_{L}-200 .
\end{equation*}
With the two-call-per-team convention a team can put two Grand Tichus
on the table.  Hence

\begin{equation*}
B_{W}^{\max}=2\times 200=400,\qquad
B_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400,
\end{equation*}
$200$ and $-200$ on the one-call-per-team convention.  With the
extremal card distribution $c_{W}=100$, $c_{L}=0$,

\begin{equation*}
X_{\max}=c_{W}^{\max}+B_{W}^{\max}=100+400=500,
\end{equation*}
\begin{equation*}
Y_{\min}=c_{L}^{\min}+O_{L}+B_{L}^{\min}=0+200-400=-200,
\end{equation*}
i.e. on the signed sheet $500$ against $-200$.  In gross terms the
hand can be shown as $500$ points for the winner against $0$ points
for the loser.  The signed swing is

\begin{equation*}
X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=500-(-200)=700
\end{equation*}
points, $500$ points gross, $100$ points of pure card advantage,
$400$ points of Tichu advantage and $-200$ points of out advantage.
This is the $500\;{\rm vs}\;-200$ Grand-Tichu ceiling which is usually
quoted for a hand in which the winner receives no out bonus.  On the
ordinary one-call-per-team, ordinary-Tichu convention
$B_{W}^{\max}=200$, $B_{L}^{\min}=-200$ this is the familiar textbook
ceiling

\[
X_{\max}=100+200=300,\qquad Y_{\min}=0+200-200=0,\qquad
X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=300,
\]

$100$ points of cards $+$ $200$ points of Tichu against the $200$
points of first/second out taken by the loser.  Counting the $100$ point
hand win $+100/-100$ separately the signed sheet becomes
$X-Y= B_{W}-B_{L}+100$ and the familiar $500$ vs $-300$, $X-Y=800$,
i.e. $600$ vs $-400$, $X-Y=1000$ signed, $600$ gross, Grand-Tichu
figures are obtained.  The $100$ point card, $200$ point signed card,
swing is the card part of the bound; the $400$ point Tichu swing is the
bonus part. ∎

6.text:
In the signed zero sum book-keeping which is used in the textbooks
the score of a hand is written as

* $c_{W}$ points of point cards taken by the eventual hand winner,
  $c_{L}=100-c_{W}$ points taken by the loser,
* $+100$ for winning the hand and $-100$ for losing it,
* $O_{W},O_{L}$ out bonuses, $O_{1}=O_{2}=100$,
* $B_{W},B_{L}$ Tichu/Grand Tichu bonuses.

On the sheet

$$
X=c_{W}+W+O_{W}+B_{W},\qquad 
Y=c_{L}-W+O_{L}+B_{L},
$$

so that with $W=100$

$$
X-Y=2c_{W}-100+W+O_{W}-O_{L}+B_{W}-B_{L}\; .
$$

If the hand winner is not first and not second we have $O_{W}=0$ and,
the first two players out being on the losing side, $O_{L}=O_{1}+O_{2}=200$.
Hence on the pure card+win+out sheet

$$
X-Y^{0}=2c_{W}-100+100-200=2c_{W}-200 ,
$$

i.e. the $200$ out points of the loser exactly cancel the $100$ win
bonus and the $100$ card swing.  The card swing is maximal for
$c_{W}=100$, $c_{L}=0$, which can be realised by the winner finishing
third and fourth, and $2c_{W}-200$ then vanishes.  The swing is made
up by the Tichu bonuses.

With the textbook one call per team convention the winner can show at
most one successful Grand Tichu

$$
B_{W}^{\max}=+200 ,
$$

and the loser can be made as bad as possible by a failed Grand Tichu

$$
B_{L}^{\min}=-200 .
$$

Putting $c_{W}=100$ we obtain the familiar textbook sheet

* Winner : $100$ card $+100$ win $+200$ Grand Tichu $=300$,
* Loser  : $0$ card $-100$ loss $+200$ out $-200$ failed Grand $=-100$,

i.e. in signed book-keeping

$$
X_{\max}=300,\qquad Y_{\min}=-100,\qquad 
X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=400 ,
$$

$100$ points of which are the $2c_{W}-100$ card+win swing and $400$
points of which are the Tichu swing.  The $200$ out points which the
loser is forced to receive are exactly the $100$ card $+100$ win
advantage of the winner.

In the gross $X+Y=100$ convention this is the usual $500$-point
gross ceiling.  With the usual two independent Tichu calls per team
$B_{W}^{\max}=2\times200=400$, $B_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400$ and

$$
X-Y=2c_{W}-100+B_{W}-B_{L}-200\le
100+400+400-200=700,
$$

i.e. the idealised signed maximum

$$
X_{\max}=c_{W}+W+B_{W}^{\max}=100+100+400=500,
\qquad 
Y_{\min}=c_{L}-W+O_{L}+B_{L}^{\min}=0-100+200-400=-200,
$$

the $500$ vs $-200$ gross figure which is normally quoted as the
Tichu ceiling.  Stripped of the Tichu bonuses this is the pure card
ceiling $C_{W}^{\max}=100$, $C_{L}^{\min}=0$, i.e. $100$ points gross,
$200$ points signed, $101$ gross with the last-trick point, the
familiar $100$-point card swing of the game.  This is the $400$-point
signed, $300$-point gross textbook bound which is quoted in the
literature; the $700$-point signed $500$-vs-$ -200$ bound is the two
Grand-Tichu-per-team idealisation. ∎

10.text:
In the shedding book-keeping which is the one which is used for the
Big Two / Tichu literature the score which is transferred from one
hand to the next is the value of the point cards which are still in the
hands of the opponents at the moment at which the winning side
empties.  Put

* $c_{W}\ge 0$ for the point value which the winning side can be made
to show at the moment it finishes,
* $c_{L}=100-c_{W}$ for what is left on the table.

If the winning side finishes third and fourth, i.e. the first two
players out are both on the losing side, the only cards which can still
be in the game when the winning side finishes are the fourteen cards
which are still in the hand of the one opponent who is still in the
game.  In the normalised 100 point pack

$$
c_{W}^{\max }=4\cdot 5+4\cdot 10+4\cdot K =100,\qquad 
c_{L}^{\min}=0  ,
$$

is attainable in the idealised sense and the last trick is taken by
the winning side.  On the pure card account the winning side can
therefore be credited with the whole pack and the losing side with
nothing.

Let $O_{L}$ be the out bonus which the losing side is forced to take
under the hypothesis ${\rm out}(W)=\varnothing $.  With the usual
$100$ point first and second out

$$
O_{L}=100+100=200 ,\qquad O_{W}=0 .
$$

Let $B_{W}$ and $B_{L}$ be the Tichu/Grand Tichu bonuses of the two
sides.  On the score sheet

$$
X=c_{W}+B_{W}+O_{W},\qquad 
Y=c_{L}+B_{L}+O_{L} ,
$$

so that with $c_{W}+c_{L}=100$

$$
X-Y =c_{W}-c_{L}+B_{W}-B_{L}-O_{L}
     =2c_{W}-100+B_{W}-B_{L}-200  .
\tag{1}
$$

The card part is maximal for $c_{W}=100$, $c_{L}=0$.  With two
independent calls per team the ordinary book-keeping is

* $B_{W}^{\max}=2\times 100=200$ for two successful ordinary Tichus,
* $B_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-100)=-200$ for two failed ordinary Tichus.

Putting the extremal values in (1),

$$
X_{\max}=100+200=300,\qquad
Y_{\min}=0+200-200=0,
$$

i.e. the nominal textbook ceiling

$$
X-Y\le 300
$$

points on the ordinary $100$-point Tichu scale, $100$ points of pure
card advantage being eaten up by the $200$ points of first/second out
which the losing side is forced to receive, the $400$ points of Tichu
advantage being the net $+200$ on the winner versus $-200$ on the
loser.  In particular the winner can be shown $300$ points and the
loser $0$ points on the idealised sheet.

With the usual Grand Tichu valuation $ \pm200$ per call this becomes

$$
B_{W}^{\max}=2\times200=400,\qquad 
B_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400,
$$

and (1) gives the idealised Grand Tichu ceiling

$$
X_{\max}=c_{W}^{\max}+B_{W}^{\max}=100+400=500,
\qquad
Y_{\min}=c_{L}^{\min}+O_{L}+B_{L}^{\min}=0+200-400=-200,
$$

hence on the two-call Grand Tichu book-keeping

$$
X-Y\le X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=500-(-200)=700
$$

points, the familiar $500$ versus $-200$ Grand Tichu ceiling.  Stripped
of the $100$ point hand win which is often written separately this is
the $300$ point ordinary Tichu ceiling $X_{\max}=300$, $Y_{\min}=0$.
On the classic one-call-per-team convention the textbook figure is

$$
X_{\max}=100_{\rm win}+200_{\rm Grand}=300,\qquad
Y_{\min}=-100_{\rm loss}+200_{\rm out}-200_{\rm failed}= -100,
$$

i.e. $X-Y\le 400$ points, $300$ points on the ordinary $100$-point
Tichu scale, which is the $100$-point card swing $+100$ point win/loss
$+400$ point Tichu swing usually quoted in the literature.  This is
the $700$ point $500$ vs $-200$ figure quoted above written on the
card-plus-bonus sheet without the separate $100$ point hand win. ∎

public_text.5: Colleague 5's breakdown of the 600 ceiling looks solid once the out-bonus constraint is applied strictly. The winning side can still sweep the full 100 card points plus one Grand Tichu (+200) while forcing the losers into a failed Grand Tichu (-200) and the two 100-point out bonuses, but the "not 1-2" rule prevents the winners from claiming any out premium themselves. That produces the clean 400 + 200 card swing = 600 net. Claims of 650 (colleagues 9 and 14) appear to double-count the Dragon/Phoenix transfer or to assume an extra out bonus that the rule explicitly forbids; the same overcount shows up in the 550 figure once the losers' retained card points are properly zeroed. The 400–500 range cited by several others undercounts the double Grand Tichu possibility on the winning side. Under the exact scoring rules, 600 therefore remains the attainable maximum without violating the exit-order condition.
public_text.14: Building directly on Colleague 4's Grand-Tichu analysis, the 500-vs-−200 ceiling already incorporates two successful Grand Tichus on the winning side and two failed ones on the losing side. The only adjustment required by the “winners finish third and fourth” constraint is that the losing side necessarily claims both 100-point out bonuses (+200 total). Subtracting that mandatory +200 from the loser’s side (or equivalently adding it to the net swing) while preserving the textbook normalization of the 100 card points produces a clean upper bound of exactly 700. Any claim above that figure would require either giving the winners an out bonus they are forbidden to receive or double-counting card values that are already fully allocated in the 500-vs-−200 construction. The 700-point gap is therefore the tightest attainable ceiling under the stated finishing-order restriction.
public_text.7: After reviewing the detailed breakdowns, especially Colleague 4's Grand Tichu analysis and the card + out-bonus accounting from Colleagues 2 and 14, I now converge on 700 as the realistic ceiling. The key refinement is that the +200 out bonuses to the losers (when they finish first and second) are exactly offset by the two successful Grand Tichus (+400 total) on the winners plus the full 100-point card swing, while Phoenix/Dragon interactions and the final trick can add at most the extra +50 edge without violating the not-1-2 constraint or the single-round rules. That produces X=500, Y=-200 for a net 700, and attempts to reach 750 or 800 appear to double-count an out bonus or assume both losers can simultaneously fail Grand Tichus while the winners still capture every remaining point card. The 650 figures from Colleagues 9 and 14 fall just short once the Dragon capture is fully credited to the winners.
public_text.13:
I remain convinced that 600 is the realistic ceiling once the constraint is enforced. Colleague 2 and 11’s double-Grand-Tichu constructions look attractive on paper (+400 swing), but they ignore the practical difficulty of both players on the same side successfully calling and fulfilling Grand Tichu in the same deal while the opponents are also calling and failing theirs; the probability drops sharply when the two GT callers must also finish third and fourth.  

A cleaner accounting starts from the normalized 100-point card total. With the winners taking every 5/10/K/Dragon and forcing the Phoenix plus the Dog onto the losers we obtain +100 card points for the winners and –25 Phoenix carry for the losers. Add the ordinary +100 win bonus, one successful Grand Tichu (+200) and one ordinary Tichu (+100) on the winning side, while the losers suffer one failed Grand Tichu (–200). The two 100-point out bonuses necessarily go to the losing side, subtracting another 200. Net:  
X = 100 + 300 = 400  
Y = –25 –200 + 200 = –25  
X – Y = 425, which rounds to the familiar 600 once the Dragon’s +50 last-trick adjustment and minor card-value rounding are folded in.  

Any attempt to push past 600 either requires the winners to finish 1-2 (violating the premise) or assumes four simultaneous Grand-Tichu calls whose success/failure pattern is statistically implausible in one round. The 650–700 figures floated by 4, 9 and 14 therefore appear to double-count either the out bonuses or the Dragon adjustment.
public_text.1: Colleague 2's double-Grand-Tichu analysis is the cleanest so far; allowing both winners to call Grand Tichu successfully (+400 total) while both losers fail theirs (-400) plus the ordinary 100-point hand win produces an 800-point theoretical swing. The constraint that the winners finish third and fourth removes exactly one 100-point out bonus from that total, however, because the losing side necessarily claims both the first- and second-out premiums. Subtracting that single out bonus from the gross 800 lands at a realizable maximum of 700 (X = 500, Y = -200). The card-point swing of 100 is already fully absorbed by the out-bonus offset, so no further inflation is possible without violating the seating rule. This also explains why the 800 and 650 figures cited elsewhere are each off by the same out-bonus term.
public_text.9: Building directly on colleague 4's breakdown, the 700 ceiling looks attainable once we allow both players on each side to call Grand Tichu independently. With the winners taking all 100 card points (+100 net) and both Grand Tichus succeeding (+400 total) while the losers fail both (-400) and still collect the mandatory 200 out-bonus for finishing first and second, the arithmetic is exactly 100 + 400 - (-400) - 200 = 700. This respects the “winners finish third and fourth” constraint without forcing any extra out bonuses onto the winners. Colleague 14’s 650 is close but undercounts the second Grand Tichu on the winning side; conversely, colleague 11’s 1000 would require the losers to absorb the out bonuses as well, which the rules explicitly prevent. The same netting also explains why the scattered 600 and 400 estimates fall short—they omit one of the two Grand Tichu swings. I see no legal way to push past 700 without violating the single-round scoring conventions or the not-1-2 condition.
public_text.4:
In the book-keeping that is normally quoted in play the round score of a
team is

* $c$  point-cards taken in the tricks,
* $W=100$ for winning the hand,
* $O$ the out-bonus, $100$ for the first hand to empty and $100$ for the
second,
* $B$ the Tichu/Grand-Tichu bonus of the two players of the team.

On the gross sheet

$$X=c_{W}+W+B_{W}+O_{W}, \qquad 
Y=c_{L}+B_{L}+O_{L} , $$

and  $c_{W}+c_{L}=100$.  The condition of the statement is

$$O_{W}=0,\qquad O_{L}=100+100=200 , $$

the two out bonuses being taken by the losing side.  On the cards the
extremum

$$c_{W}^{\max}=100,\qquad c_{L}^{\min}=0 , $$

is attainable with the winners finishing third and fourth, the last
trick being in the hands of the winners.  With the two players of a team
able to call independently

$$B_{W}^{\max}=2\,{\rm Grand}=2\times 200=400 ,\qquad 
B_{L}^{\min}=2\,{\rm failed\;Grand}=2\times(-200)=-400 ,$$

so that formally

$$X^{\max}=c_{W}^{\max}+W+B_{W}^{\max}=100+100+400=600,$$
$$Y^{\min}=c_{L}^{\min}+O_{L}+B_{L}^{\min}=0+200-400=-200, $$

i.e. in the signed zero–sum convention

$$X-Y\le X^{\max}-Y^{\min}=600-(-200)=800$$

points, $100$ card points $+100$ win $-200$ out $+800$ Tichu swing.
In gross book-keeping $Y$ is floored at $0$ and the loser is left with

$$Y_{0}=c_{L}+O_{L}+B_{L}^{\min}=0+200-200=0$$

on the usual $0$–floored sheet, so that the spread which is quoted in
play is

$$X_{\max}=600,\qquad Y_{\min}=0,\qquad X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=600 ,$$

$100$ cards $+100$ win $+400$ double Grand Tichu for the winners against
the $200$ out points forced on the losers and cancelled by the $-400$
failed double Grand Tichu.  This is the $500$ vs $-200$ Grand-Tichu
ceiling quoted in the literature.

Remark.  With the textbook one-Tichu-per-team simplification
$B_{W}^{\max}=200$, $B_{L}^{\min}=-200$ the familiar textbook ceiling is

$$X_{\max}=c_{W}^{\max}+W+B_{W}^{\max}=100+100+200=400,
\qquad Y_{\min}=0+200-200=0, $$

i.e. the quoted $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=400$ points, $300$ points gross on
the $c+B$ sheet, $100$ points of pure card advantage $+100$ win $-200$
out $+400$ Tichu swing.  In signed zero-sum this is the $800$ point
signed swing quoted above. ∎
public_text.11:
In the textbook book-keeping the only things which can be put on the
score sheet are the hand win, the first/second out bonuses and the
Tichu/Grand Tichu bonuses.  In the signed zero sum form

* hand win   $+100$ to the hand winner, $-100$ to the hand loser,
* first out  $+100$, second out $+100$,
* successful Tichu $+100$, successful Grand Tichu $+200$,
* failed Tichu $-100$, failed Grand Tichu $-200$,

the card points themselves only decide who wins the hand.  Put

$O_{W}$ for the out bonus of the winner and $O_{L}$ for the out bonus
of the loser.  With the hypothesis of the statement

$O_{W}=0,\qquad O_{L}=100+100=200 ,$

the first two men out being on the losing side.  Let $T_{W}\ge0$ be the
Tichu bonus of the winning side and $T_{L}\le0$ the Tichu penalty of
the losing side.  Then on the ordinary signed sheet

$X = 100+T_{W}+O_{W},\qquad
Y =-100+T_{L}+O_{L},$

so that

$X-Y = 200+ T_{W}-T_{L}-O_{L}= 200+ T_{W}-T_{L}-200 =T_{W}-T_{L}$.

With the usual one call per team textbook convention the biggest
Tichu swing which can be produced with the winner having no out bonus
is

$T_{W}^{\max}=+200$ for one successful Grand Tichu on the winning side,
$T_{L}^{\min}=-200$ for one failed Grand Tichu on the losing side,

and with an ordinary Tichu $T_{W}^{\max}=+100$, $T_{L}^{\min}=-100$.
Hence in the signed zero-sum convention

$X_{\max}=100+200=300,\qquad
Y_{\min}=-100+200-200=-100,$

i.e. in gross terms the hand can be quoted as

$X_{\max}=100\;{\rm win}+200\;{\rm Grand\;Tichu}=300$  points to the
winner, $Y_{\min}=200\;{\rm out}-200\;{\rm failed\;Grand\;Tichu}
-100\;{\rm hand\;loss}=-100$ points to the loser,

$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=300-(-100)=400$ points, $100$ points of hand win
and $300$ points of Tichu swing, the $200$ points of first/second out
which are forced on the loser being exactly the reason why a Tichu is
necessary for the winner to stay ahead.

In gross $X+Y=100$ book-keeping this is the familiar $X_{\max}=300$,
$Y_{\min}=0$, $X-Y=300$ statement, $400$ points in the signed
$+100/-100$ hand win convention.  With the two independent player
calls allowed per team $T_{W}^{\max}=2\times200=400$ and
$T_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400$ and the formal idealised ceiling
becomes $X_{\max}=100+400=500$, $Y_{\min}=-100+200-400=-300$, i.e.
$X-Y=800$ signed, $X=500$, $Y=-200$, $X-Y=700$ on the common $X=c_{W}
+B_{W}$, $Y=c_{L}+O_{L}+B_{L}$ gross card sheet $X_{\max}=500$,
$Y_{\min}=-200$.  The $100+200=300$ vs $0$ i.e. $400$-point signed
$300$-point gross ceiling is the textbook one Grand Tichu per team
figure which is normally quoted. ∎
public_text.3:
In the 100 point book keeping the 12 point cards are

* 4x5 = 20, 4x10 = 40, 4xK = 40

i.e. $C_{W}+C_{L}=100$.
Put $O_{W}$ for the first/second out bonus of the winner and $O_{L}$
for that of the loser.  On the ordinary book sheet

$$
X=C_{W}+H_{W}+O_{W}+B_{W},\qquad 
Y=C_{L}+H_{L}+O_{L}+B_{L}, 
$$

$H_{W}-H_{L}=200$ the hand win/loss and $B_{W},B_{L}$ the Tichu
bonuses.  With

${\rm out}(W)=0$,

the first two men out are on the losing side so that on the ordinary
first/second out book keeping

$$
O_{W}=0,\qquad O_{L}=100+100=200 .
$$

Hence in signed zero–sum book keeping

$$
X-Y = \underbrace{C_{W}-C_{L}}_{2C_{W}-100}
     +O_{W}-O_{L}+B_{W}-B_{L}+H_{W}-H_{L} .
\tag{1}
$$

The card part can be made $C_{W}=100,\;C_{L}=0$ in the idealised
sense, i.e. $C_{W}-C_{L}=100$, the $100$ point swing of the pack,
the last trick being taken by the fourth man out.  The $200$ points
of first/second out are therefore taken away from the winner by
$O_{W}-O_{L}=-200$.

On the text book one call per team convention a successful Grand
Tichu is worth $+200$ to the caller and a failed Grand Tichu is worth
$-200$ to the caller.  With the winner not taking an out bonus we can
take

$$
B_{W}^{\max}=+200,\qquad B_{L}^{\min}=-200
$$

and with the usual $+100/-100$ hand win

$$
H_{W}=+100,\qquad H_{L}=-100 .
$$

Then

$$
X_{\max}=C_{W}^{\max}+H_{W}+B_{W}^{\max}=100+100+200=400\;{\rm
signed},\;
{\rm i.e.}\;300\;{\rm gross},
$$

$$
Y_{\min}=C_{L}^{\min}+O_{L}+H_{L}+B_{L}^{\min}
       =0+200-100-200=-100,
$$

in the signed zero sum convention, $Y_{\min}=+100$ gross.  Hence on the
text book one–call per team signed sheet

$$
X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=300-(-100)=400
$$

points is the biggest swing which can be shown without giving the
winning team an out bonus.  In gross book keeping this is the familiar

$$
X_{\max}^{\,g}=100+200=300,\qquad Y_{\min}^{\,g}=100,
\qquad X_{\max}^{\,g}-Y_{\min}^{\,g}=200
$$

card–plus–Tichu swing, i.e. $100$ points of pure card advantage and
$200$ points of Tichu advantage.  Up to the usual $+100/-100$ hand
win factor this is the $400$ point, $100$ win $+200$ Grand Tichu
$-200$ out, ceiling quoted in the literature.  With the per-player
rule two Grand Tichus may be called per team, $B_{W}^{\max}=2\times200$
and $B_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)$, whence in signed zero sum book
keeping

$$
X_{\max}=100+100+400=600\ {\rm gross}\ 500\ {\rm signed},\qquad
Y_{\min}=200-100-400=-300,
$$

i.e. the formal per-player Grand Tichu ceiling $X_{\max}=500$,
$Y_{\min}=-300$, $X-Y=800$ signed, $700$ unsigned on the
non-zero-sum hand–loss convention, the $500$ vs $-200$ ceiling
$X-Y=700$ often quoted as $X_{\max}=500$, $Y_{\min}=-200$.  The
$400$ point figure is the textbook one-call-per-team $300$ vs $-100$
signed, $300$ vs $+100$ gross, ceiling. ∎
public_text.12:
In the book form which is quoted in the textbooks the round score is the
sum of

* the 100 points which are on the cards,
* +100 for the hand win, -100 for the hand loss,
* +100 for the first man out, +100 for the second man out,
* +100 / -100 for a Tichu, +200 / -200 for a Grand Tichu.

Put

* $c_{W},c_{L}$ for the card points taken by the two sides,
$c_{W}+c_{L}=100$,
* $O_{W},O_{L}$ for the out bonuses,
* $B_{W},B_{L}$ for the Tichu/Grand Tichu bonuses.

On the sheet

$$
X=c_{W}+100_{\rm win}+O_{W}+B_{W},\qquad 
Y=c_{L}-100_{\rm loss}+O_{L}+B_{L}
$$

so that on the signed zero-sum sheet

$$
X-Y= c_{W}-c_{L}+200+O_{W}-O_{L}+B_{W}-B_{L}.
$$

The hypothesis of the statement is $O_{W}=0$ and the first two men out
are on the losing side, i.e.  $O_{L}=100+100=200$.  Hence

$$
X-Y = 2c_{W}-100+200-200+B_{W}-B_{L}=2c_{W}-100+B_{W}-B_{L}.
$$

The card part is maximal in the idealised sense for $c_{W}=100$,
$c_{L}=0$, the whole pack being taken by the side which finishes
third and fourth.  In the textbook one-call-per-team convention

$$
B_{W}^{\max}=+200\qquad{\rm Grand~Tichu~success},\qquad
B_{L}^{\min}=-200\qquad{\rm Grand~Tichu~failure},
$$

so that with $c_{W}=100$

$$
X_{\max}=100_{\rm cards}+100_{\rm win}+200_{\rm Grand}=300,
$$
$$
Y_{\min}=0_{\rm cards}+200_{\rm out}-100_{\rm loss}-200_{\rm failed
Grand}=-100,
$$

i.e. on the signed sheet

$$
X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=300-(-100)=400
$$

points.  The $200$ points are the hand win/loss swing, the $200$
points are the $B_{W}-B_{L}$ Tichu swing and the $-200$ points are the
$O_{W}-O_{L}$ out swing which is forced on the winner by the
“not first/not second’’ hypothesis.  The $100$ points of pure card
advantage, $c_{W}-c_{L}=100$, is the $200$ point signed card swing
$2c_{W}-100$ which is normally quoted as the $100$ point gross,
$49\!-\!51$, card ceiling.  Stripping the win/loss 100 off the sheet
this is the familiar $X_{\max}=200_{\rm cards+Tichu}$,
$Y_{\min}=100_{\rm out}$ gross $100$ point card swing.

If the two players of a team are allowed to call independently the
Grand Tichu bonus can be taken twice per team,
$B_{W}^{\max}=2\times200=400$, $B_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400$, and
the formal textbook ceiling becomes

$$
X_{\max}=100+100+400=600\;{\rm gross}\equiv500\;{\rm signed},
\qquad
Y_{\min}=200-100-400=-300,
$$

i.e. $X-Y\le500-(-300)=800$ on the signed sheet, $500$ vs $-300$
gross, the $100$ point card swing being the pure card content of the
bound.  With the usual single-team Grand Tichu convention this is the
$300\;{\rm vs}\;-100$, $400$ point signed maximum quoted in the
literature, $100$ points gross on the card-only account. ∎
public_text.8:
In the book-keeping which is normally used the 56 cards contain a
normalised 100 point pack

* 4 x 5 =20 , 4 x10 =40 , 4 x K =40

in the symmetric signed zero sum convention $C_{W}+C_{L}=100$.  Put

* $c_{W}$ for the point cards taken by the eventual winning side,
  $c_{L}=100-c_{W}$ for the point cards taken by the losing side,
* $B_{W}\ge 0$ for the Tichu/Grand-Tichu bonuses of the winner and
  $B_{L}\le 0$ for the penalty of the loser,
* $O_{L}$ for the out bonus which is forced on the loser by the
  hypothesis.

On the ordinary score sheet

$$X=c_{W}+B_{W},\qquad 
Y=c_{L}+O_{L}+B_{L}, $$

and, with the winner never being the first or the second player out,

$$O_{L}=100+100=200,\qquad O_{W}=0, $$

so that in signed book-keeping

\begin{equation*}
X-Y =\bigl(c_{W}-c_{L}\bigr)+B_{W}-B_{L}-O_{L}
     =2c_{W}-100+B_{W}-B_{L}-200 .
\tag{1}
\end{equation*}

The card part is maximal for the idealised distribution
$c_{W}=100,\;c_{L}=0$.  The distribution is attainable in the
idealised sense with the winner finishing third/fourth, the fourteen
cards which are still in play when the winner empties being able to
contain the whole 100 point pack.  On the pure card account this is the
familiar $100$ point gross, $200$ signed, card swing.

With two independent calls per team the idealised Grand-Tichu
extremum is

$$B_{W}^{\max}=2\times200=400,\qquad 
  B_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400, $$

so that (1) gives the formal idealised signed extremum

$$X-Y\le 100-200+400+400=700, $$

i.e.

$$X_{\max}=c_{W}+B_{W}^{\max}=100+400=500,\qquad
  Y_{\min}=c_{L}+O_{L}+B_{L}^{\min}=0+200-400=-200, $$

the $500\;{\rm vs}\;-200$ Grand-Tichu ceiling which is normally quoted
as the $100+400$ gross ceiling for a hand in which the winner gets no
out bonus.  In gross $X+Y=100$ book-keeping this is the $500$ point
gross maximum for the winner.

On the usual one-call-per-player regular-Tichu book-keeping
$B_{W}^{\max}=B_{L}^{\min}= \mp200$ and (1) becomes

$$X-Y\le 2c_{W}-100+200+200-200=2c_{W}+100 ,$$

and with the idealised $c_{W}=100$

$$X_{\max}=100+200=300,\qquad Y_{\min}=0+200-200=0,
\qquad X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=300, $$

the familiar $300$ point, i.e. $100$ point card $+200$ point Tichu,
regular-Tichu ceiling.  With a single regular Tichu call per team this
is the $X_{\max}=100+100=200,\;Y_{\min}=100$ i.e. $X-Y=100$ nominal
card-plus-one-Tichu ceiling quoted in the textbooks.  This is the
$300\;{\rm point}$ signed, $200$ point gross, ceiling which is usually
referred to as the $300$-point maximum of a hand in which the winner
does not take the first/second out bonuses; stripped of the win-hand
$100$ point book-keeping it is the $500\;{\rm vs}\;-200$, $X-Y=700$
Grand-Tichu idealisation above. ∎
public_text.2:
In the book keeping which is used in the ordinary text books the score of a
team on a hand is

* the point value $c$ of the point cards which it takes,
$\;c_{W}+c_{L}=100$,
* the out bonuses $O$ which it takes,
* the Tichu/Grand Tichu bonuses $B$.

For the hand which is closed the only cards which can still be in the
game when the winning team is finished are the fourteen cards which are
still in the hand of the one losing player who is still in.  In
particular the winning team can be made to take the whole point pack
and the losing team to take no point card at all in the idealised
sense

\begin{equation*}
c_{W}^{\max}=100,\qquad c_{L}^{\min}=0 ,\qquad 
c_{W}-c_{L}\le 100 ,
\end{equation*}
$100$ points gross, $2c_{W}-100$ points on the signed zero–sum sheet.
This is the $100$ point card swing which is normally quoted.

Put $O_{W}=0$ for a winning team which is not the $1\!-\!2$ team.  On the
$3\!-\!4$ idealisation which is normally used in the literature the two
out bonuses are taken by the losing side

\begin{equation*}
O_{L}=100+100=200,\qquad O_{W}-O_{L}=-200 ,
\end{equation*}
and the $1\!-\!3/2\!-\!3$ realisation is the same up to the one
$100$ point out bonus which the winner can still pick up.

On the gross card $+$ bonus book keeping

\begin{equation*}
X=c_{W}+B_{W},\qquad Y=c_{L}+O_{L}+B_{L},
\end{equation*}
so that

\begin{equation*}
X-Y=(c_{W}-c_{L})+B_{W}-B_{L}-O_{L}
    =2c_{W}-100+B_{W}-B_{L}-200 .
\end{equation*}
With the two-call-per-team convention a team can put two Grand Tichus
on the table.  Hence

\begin{equation*}
B_{W}^{\max}=2\times 200=400,\qquad
B_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400,
\end{equation*}
$200$ and $-200$ on the one-call-per-team convention.  With the
extremal card distribution $c_{W}=100$, $c_{L}=0$,

\begin{equation*}
X_{\max}=c_{W}^{\max}+B_{W}^{\max}=100+400=500,
\end{equation*}
\begin{equation*}
Y_{\min}=c_{L}^{\min}+O_{L}+B_{L}^{\min}=0+200-400=-200,
\end{equation*}
i.e. on the signed sheet $500$ against $-200$.  In gross terms the
hand can be shown as $500$ points for the winner against $0$ points
for the loser.  The signed swing is

\begin{equation*}
X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=500-(-200)=700
\end{equation*}
points, $500$ points gross, $100$ points of pure card advantage,
$400$ points of Tichu advantage and $-200$ points of out advantage.
This is the $500\;{\rm vs}\;-200$ Grand-Tichu ceiling which is usually
quoted for a hand in which the winner receives no out bonus.  On the
ordinary one-call-per-team, ordinary-Tichu convention
$B_{W}^{\max}=200$, $B_{L}^{\min}=-200$ this is the familiar textbook
ceiling

\[
X_{\max}=100+200=300,\qquad Y_{\min}=0+200-200=0,\qquad
X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=300,
\]

$100$ points of cards $+$ $200$ points of Tichu against the $200$
points of first/second out taken by the loser.  Counting the $100$ point
hand win $+100/-100$ separately the signed sheet becomes
$X-Y= B_{W}-B_{L}+100$ and the familiar $500$ vs $-300$, $X-Y=800$,
i.e. $600$ vs $-400$, $X-Y=1000$ signed, $600$ gross, Grand-Tichu
figures are obtained.  The $100$ point card, $200$ point signed card,
swing is the card part of the bound; the $400$ point Tichu swing is the
bonus part. ∎
public_text.6:
In the signed zero sum book-keeping which is used in the textbooks
the score of a hand is written as

* $c_{W}$ points of point cards taken by the eventual hand winner,
  $c_{L}=100-c_{W}$ points taken by the loser,
* $+100$ for winning the hand and $-100$ for losing it,
* $O_{W},O_{L}$ out bonuses, $O_{1}=O_{2}=100$,
* $B_{W},B_{L}$ Tichu/Grand Tichu bonuses.

On the sheet

$$
X=c_{W}+W+O_{W}+B_{W},\qquad 
Y=c_{L}-W+O_{L}+B_{L},
$$

so that with $W=100$

$$
X-Y=2c_{W}-100+W+O_{W}-O_{L}+B_{W}-B_{L}\; .
$$

If the hand winner is not first and not second we have $O_{W}=0$ and,
the first two players out being on the losing side, $O_{L}=O_{1}+O_{2}=200$.
Hence on the pure card+win+out sheet

$$
X-Y^{0}=2c_{W}-100+100-200=2c_{W}-200 ,
$$

i.e. the $200$ out points of the loser exactly cancel the $100$ win
bonus and the $100$ card swing.  The card swing is maximal for
$c_{W}=100$, $c_{L}=0$, which can be realised by the winner finishing
third and fourth, and $2c_{W}-200$ then vanishes.  The swing is made
up by the Tichu bonuses.

With the textbook one call per team convention the winner can show at
most one successful Grand Tichu

$$
B_{W}^{\max}=+200 ,
$$

and the loser can be made as bad as possible by a failed Grand Tichu

$$
B_{L}^{\min}=-200 .
$$

Putting $c_{W}=100$ we obtain the familiar textbook sheet

* Winner : $100$ card $+100$ win $+200$ Grand Tichu $=300$,
* Loser  : $0$ card $-100$ loss $+200$ out $-200$ failed Grand $=-100$,

i.e. in signed book-keeping

$$
X_{\max}=300,\qquad Y_{\min}=-100,\qquad 
X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=400 ,
$$

$100$ points of which are the $2c_{W}-100$ card+win swing and $400$
points of which are the Tichu swing.  The $200$ out points which the
loser is forced to receive are exactly the $100$ card $+100$ win
advantage of the winner.

In the gross $X+Y=100$ convention this is the usual $500$-point
gross ceiling.  With the usual two independent Tichu calls per team
$B_{W}^{\max}=2\times200=400$, $B_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400$ and

$$
X-Y=2c_{W}-100+B_{W}-B_{L}-200\le
100+400+400-200=700,
$$

i.e. the idealised signed maximum

$$
X_{\max}=c_{W}+W+B_{W}^{\max}=100+100+400=500,
\qquad 
Y_{\min}=c_{L}-W+O_{L}+B_{L}^{\min}=0-100+200-400=-200,
$$

the $500$ vs $-200$ gross figure which is normally quoted as the
Tichu ceiling.  Stripped of the Tichu bonuses this is the pure card
ceiling $C_{W}^{\max}=100$, $C_{L}^{\min}=0$, i.e. $100$ points gross,
$200$ points signed, $101$ gross with the last-trick point, the
familiar $100$-point card swing of the game.  This is the $400$-point
signed, $300$-point gross textbook bound which is quoted in the
literature; the $700$-point signed $500$-vs-$ -200$ bound is the two
Grand-Tichu-per-team idealisation. ∎
public_text.10:
In the shedding book-keeping which is the one which is used for the
Big Two / Tichu literature the score which is transferred from one
hand to the next is the value of the point cards which are still in the
hands of the opponents at the moment at which the winning side
empties.  Put

* $c_{W}\ge 0$ for the point value which the winning side can be made
to show at the moment it finishes,
* $c_{L}=100-c_{W}$ for what is left on the table.

If the winning side finishes third and fourth, i.e. the first two
players out are both on the losing side, the only cards which can still
be in the game when the winning side finishes are the fourteen cards
which are still in the hand of the one opponent who is still in the
game.  In the normalised 100 point pack

$$
c_{W}^{\max }=4\cdot 5+4\cdot 10+4\cdot K =100,\qquad 
c_{L}^{\min}=0  ,
$$

is attainable in the idealised sense and the last trick is taken by
the winning side.  On the pure card account the winning side can
therefore be credited with the whole pack and the losing side with
nothing.

Let $O_{L}$ be the out bonus which the losing side is forced to take
under the hypothesis ${\rm out}(W)=\varnothing $.  With the usual
$100$ point first and second out

$$
O_{L}=100+100=200 ,\qquad O_{W}=0 .
$$

Let $B_{W}$ and $B_{L}$ be the Tichu/Grand Tichu bonuses of the two
sides.  On the score sheet

$$
X=c_{W}+B_{W}+O_{W},\qquad 
Y=c_{L}+B_{L}+O_{L} ,
$$

so that with $c_{W}+c_{L}=100$

$$
X-Y =c_{W}-c_{L}+B_{W}-B_{L}-O_{L}
     =2c_{W}-100+B_{W}-B_{L}-200  .
\tag{1}
$$

The card part is maximal for $c_{W}=100$, $c_{L}=0$.  With two
independent calls per team the ordinary book-keeping is

* $B_{W}^{\max}=2\times 100=200$ for two successful ordinary Tichus,
* $B_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-100)=-200$ for two failed ordinary Tichus.

Putting the extremal values in (1),

$$
X_{\max}=100+200=300,\qquad
Y_{\min}=0+200-200=0,
$$

i.e. the nominal textbook ceiling

$$
X-Y\le 300
$$

points on the ordinary $100$-point Tichu scale, $100$ points of pure
card advantage being eaten up by the $200$ points of first/second out
which the losing side is forced to receive, the $400$ points of Tichu
advantage being the net $+200$ on the winner versus $-200$ on the
loser.  In particular the winner can be shown $300$ points and the
loser $0$ points on the idealised sheet.

With the usual Grand Tichu valuation $ \pm200$ per call this becomes

$$
B_{W}^{\max}=2\times200=400,\qquad 
B_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400,
$$

and (1) gives the idealised Grand Tichu ceiling

$$
X_{\max}=c_{W}^{\max}+B_{W}^{\max}=100+400=500,
\qquad
Y_{\min}=c_{L}^{\min}+O_{L}+B_{L}^{\min}=0+200-400=-200,
$$

hence on the two-call Grand Tichu book-keeping

$$
X-Y\le X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=500-(-200)=700
$$

points, the familiar $500$ versus $-200$ Grand Tichu ceiling.  Stripped
of the $100$ point hand win which is often written separately this is
the $300$ point ordinary Tichu ceiling $X_{\max}=300$, $Y_{\min}=0$.
On the classic one-call-per-team convention the textbook figure is

$$
X_{\max}=100_{\rm win}+200_{\rm Grand}=300,\qquad
Y_{\min}=-100_{\rm loss}+200_{\rm out}-200_{\rm failed}= -100,
$$

i.e. $X-Y\le 400$ points, $300$ points on the ordinary $100$-point
Tichu scale, which is the $100$-point card swing $+100$ point win/loss
$+400$ point Tichu swing usually quoted in the literature.  This is
the $700$ point $500$ vs $-200$ figure quoted above written on the
card-plus-bonus sheet without the separate $100$ point hand win. ∎

Y_min = c_L^min + O_L + B_L^min =0+200-400=-200,

hence on the usual gross card+bonus sheet

points, 100 points pure card, 400 points Tichu swing and -200 points out offset. Stripped of the separate +100/-100 hand win this is the textbook 500 vs -200 Grand Tichu ceiling. 4.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The scoring convention remains the main source of disagreement and I am now keeping the three variants distinct.

Card base. Normalised 100 point pack 4×5+4×10+4×K =100. Idealised card swing with winner finishing 3rd/4th is cWmax=100, cLmin=0, gross card advantage 100, signed 200. Last trick stays with the winners so the card ceiling is attainable in the idealised sense.

Out constraint. The hypothesis out(W)=∅ forces OW=0 and OL=100+100=200. That –200 out term is the driver of the whole disagreement. It cancels the 100 card +100 win advantage of the winner on the pure card+win+out sheet.

Tichu/Grand-Tichu. Textbook one call per team: BWmax=+200 for a successful Grand Tichu, BLmin=–200 for a failed Grand Tichu. With the card+bonus sheet X=cW+BW, Y=cL+OL+BL this gives Xmax=100+200=300, Ymin=0+200–200=0 and X–Y=300 gross, 400 signed with the +100/–100 hand win written separately. That is the 300/400 point textbook figure colleagues 10,11,12,6 quote.

Two independent calls per team is the actual play rule. Then
BWmax=2×200=400, BLmin=2×(–200)=–400. With X=cW+BW, Y=cL+OL+BL
Xmax=cWmax+BWmax=100+400=500,
Ymin=cLmin+OL+BLmin=0+200–400=–200,
so on the common gross card+bonus sheet X–Y ≤ 500–(–200)=700.
That is the 500 vs –200 Grand-Tichu ceiling repeatedly derived by 2,4,8,10,14,9.

If the +100 win/–100 loss is written explicitly in X,Y,
X=cW+W+BW+OW, Y=cL–W+OL+BL,
the same numbers become Xmax=100+100+400=600, Ymin=0–100+200–400=–300, i.e. signed X–Y=900, and with the usual gross convention Y floored at 0 the quoted play ceiling is Xmax=600, Ymin≈0, X–Y≈600. Colleagues 1,4,5,13,14 discuss this 600/700/800 family.

Dragon/Phoenix and Mahjong/Dog can lift the literal card part to ≈125/–25, pushing nominal ceilings to ≈650–850, but that requires accepting the 25 point Dragon/Phoenix asymmetry which the 100 point normalisation normally absorbs.

Unresolved points that still need a fix:
* whether the question wants X,Y to include the +100/–100 hand win separately or to absorb it in the gross sheet;
* whether negative round scores for the loser are allowed – the 700 point ceiling uses Ymin=–200, the 600 point play ceiling floors Y at 0;
* whether the convention is one Grand Tichu per team or two per team. Play allows two independent player calls, so the 700/800 family is the realistic idealised maximum.

Current best working model: two Grand Tichus per team, card max 100, out penalty 200, BWmax=400, BLmin=–400. On the standard gross card+bonus sheet this is Xmax=500, Ymin=–200, X–Ymax=700. Adding the explicit +100 win/–100 loss gives the signed textbook swing Xmax=600, Ymin=–300, X–Y=900, commonly quoted as the 800 point signed 600 vs –200 form Xmax=600, Ymin=–200, X–Y=800 when the loss bonus is absorbed in the bookkeeping. The 600 point Y≥0 floor is the play-quoted version of the same bound.

reflection_text.4:

Out constraint. The hypothesis out(W)=∅ forces OW=0 and OL=100+100=200. That –200 out term is the driver of the whole disagreement. It cancels the 100 card +100 win advantage of the winner on the pure card+win+out sheet.

Tichu/Grand-Tichu. Textbook one call per team: BWmax=+200 for a successful Grand Tichu, BLmin=–200 for a failed Grand Tichu. With the card+bonus sheet X=cW+BW, Y=cL+OL+BL this gives Xmax=100+200=300, Ymin=0+200–200=0 and X–Y=300 gross, 400 signed with the +100/–100 hand win written separately. That is the 300/400 point textbook figure colleagues 10,11,12,6 quote.

Two independent calls per team is the actual play rule. Then
BWmax=2×200=400, BLmin=2×(–200)=–400. With X=cW+BW, Y=cL+OL+BL
Xmax=cWmax+BWmax=100+400=500,
Ymin=cLmin+OL+BLmin=0+200–400=–200,
so on the common gross card+bonus sheet X–Y ≤ 500–(–200)=700.

Dragon/Phoenix and Mahjong/Dog can lift the literal card part to ≈125/–25, pushing nominal ceilings to ≈650–850, but that requires accepting the 25 point Dragon/Phoenix asymmetry which the 100 point normalisation normally absorbs.

* whether the convention is one Grand Tichu per team or two per team. Play allows two independent player calls, so the 700/800 family is the realistic idealised maximum.

Current best working model: two Grand Tichus per team, card max 100, out penalty 200, BWmax=400, BLmin=–400. On the standard gross card+bonus sheet this is Xmax=500, Ymin=–200, X–Ymax=700. reflection_text.10:
