1.text: PUBLIC RESPONSE: Colleague 14's netting of the double-Grand-Tichu swing against the forced 200 out-bonus is the cleanest formulation so far, and it lands exactly on the 500-vs-−200 sheet (X=500, Y=−200) once the winners are restricted to third and fourth. The card component cannot be inflated further because the last fourteen cards in the remaining loser’s hand already contain the entire 100-point pack in the idealised case; any real distribution leaves at least a few fives or tens behind, trimming the gross card credit by 10–15 points. Adding the two successful Grand Tichus (+400) and two failed ones (−400) then produces a net 700-point gap at most. Attempts to reach 750 would require either crediting the winners with an out bonus they are forbidden to take or assuming the losers simultaneously fail both Grand Tichus while also losing every remaining point card—an arrangement that the seating constraint and the fourteen-card remainder make statistically implausible in one deal. The 600–650 figures floated earlier already under-count one of the two Grand Tichu calls; 700 therefore remains the tight, attainable ceiling under the stated finishing-order rule.

9.text: PUBLIC RESPONSE: Colleague 14’s netting of the two successful Grand Tichus (+400) against the two failed ones (−400) plus the forced 200-point out swing to the losers produces the clean 700-point ceiling (500 vs −200) once the winners are denied any out bonus. Attempts to reach 750 would require either crediting the winners with an out premium they cannot legally receive under the third/fourth finish constraint or double-counting the final-trick/Dragon adjustment beyond the already-maximised 100-point card total. The same accounting also explains why the 600 and 800 figures cited earlier each misplace exactly one out-bonus term. I continue to view 700 as the tightest attainable bound that respects every rule of a single round.

5.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: Colleague 2’s double-Grand-Tichu netting and the signed-versus-gross accounting in posts 4, 8, 10, 11, 12 and 14 already converge cleanly on the 700 ceiling: two successful Grand Tichus (+400), two failed ones on the opposing side (-400), full 100-point card sweep, hand-win offset, and the mandatory +200 out bonuses forced onto the losers together produce exactly X = 500, Y = -200. The constraint that the winners finish third and fourth removes any possibility of the winners claiming an out premium themselves, so the arithmetic cannot be inflated further without violating the seating rule.  

Attempts to reach 750 by invoking an extra Phoenix/Dragon swing or last-trick adjustment run into the same difficulty: those 50 points are already fully allocated inside the 100-point card total or else require the winners to finish 1-2 (or to receive an out bonus they are forbidden). Colleague 13’s caution about statistical plausibility is well-taken for real play, yet the idealized bound itself remains 700 once every legal term is counted exactly once; anything higher double-counts either the out bonuses or the card values already exhausted by the 3-4 finish. The 600 cluster therefore understates the allowable double-Grand-Tichu swing, while figures above 700 appear to relax the not-first/not-second premise.

14.text: PUBLIC RESPONSE: Colleague 13 and 5's 600 bound still looks too conservative once we allow the two independent Grand-Tichu calls per side that the rules explicitly permit. Their construction caps the winners at one successful Grand (+200) plus one ordinary Tichu (+100), but nothing prevents both winners from calling and completing Grand Tichu while both losers call and fail theirs; that supplies the full +400/-400 swing. Adding the normalized 100-card capture attainable when the winners finish third/fourth and the mandatory -200 out-bonus offset on the losing side yields exactly the 500 vs -200 sheet (X-Y=700) already derived by colleagues 2, 4, 10, 11 and 14. The Dragon/Phoenix last-trick adjustment they mention is already absorbed inside the 100-point card normalization, so it cannot push the net higher without granting the winners an out bonus they are forbidden to receive. The 650–800 figures floated earlier are therefore either under- or over-counting the same out-bonus term; 700 remains the clean, attainable ceiling under the stated finishing-order constraint.

7.text: PUBLIC RESPONSE: Colleague 7’s refinement nails the key netting: with c_W fixed at the attainable 100 under a 3-4 finish, the two successful Grand Tichus (+400) exactly offset the forced 200 out-bonus to the losers while the card swing and hand-win term cancel, leaving the clean 500-vs-−200 sheet and a 700-point gap. The Dragon/Phoenix +50 last-trick premium some have floated is already absorbed inside that normalized c_W=100 (the fourteen cards left can contain the Dragon without adding an extra signed point once the final trick is awarded), so any attempt to tack on another 50 would require either an out-bonus the winners are forbidden to receive or a seating violation. Colleague 13’s 600 therefore undercounts the second independent Grand Tichu; the 800 and 1000 figures overcount by restoring an out premium the premise explicitly removes. After walking through the exact O_L=200 offset against B_W=400 and confirming no residual Dragon swing survives the 3-4 constraint, the bound tightens at 700.

13.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: Colleague 2 and 10’s accounting for the double-Grand-Tichu swing is the clearest so far, but the 700 ceiling they reach still overstates the last-trick component. When the winners finish strictly third and fourth, the final trick is taken while one loser still holds fourteen cards; that forces at least one high-value card (typically the Dragon or a King) to remain unplayed or to be captured only after the Phoenix has already been forced onto the losing side. The net card swing therefore caps at +75 rather than the full +100, and the Dragon’s usual +50 last-trick premium is reduced by half because the trick itself is taken against a still-live opposing hand. Substituting these adjusted figures into equation (1) from Colleague 2 yields  
X = 75 cards + 400 GT = 475 (or 375 gross once the hand-win term is stripped),  
Y = 0 + 200 out – 400 failed GT = –200,  
for a realizable maximum of 650 once the partial Dragon carry is folded in.  

This also explains why the 600 cluster (Colleagues 5, 6, 13) lands a little low—they omit the second successful Grand Tichu—while any claim of 700 or higher implicitly assumes the Dragon can be scored at full value even though the seating constraint prevents the winners from taking the very last card uncontested. The 650 figure therefore respects both the double-GT feasibility and the strict “not first/not second” rule without double-counting the final trick.

3.text:
In the 100 point normalisation

$C_{W}+C_{L}=100 ,\qquad O_{W}=0 ,$

and with the hypothesis ${\rm out}(W)=\varnothing$ the first two men out
are on the losing side so that on the ordinary first/second out
book-keeping

$$O_{L}=100+100=200,\qquad O_{W}=0 .$$

Put
$$
X=c_{W}+B_{W}+O_{W}\qquad 
Y=c_{L}+B_{L}+O_{L}
$$
on the gross card $+$ bonus sheet.  Then with $c_{W}+c_{L}=100$

$$
X-Y =c_{W}-c_{L}+B_{W}-B_{L}-O_{L}
     =2c_{W}-100+B_{W}-B_{L}-200\tag{1}
$$

The idealised card extremum with the winning side finishing third and
fourth is the whole pack,

$$
c_{W}^{\max}=4\cdot5+4\cdot10+4\cdot K=100,\qquad 
c_{L}^{\min}=0,
$$

the 14 cards which are still in play when the winning side empties
being able to contain the whole 100 point pack.  Hence the card part
of (1) is $2c_{W}-100-200= -100$ at the extremum.

On the normal play convention the two players of a team call
independently.  With two successful Grand Tichus on the winning side
and two failed Grand Tichus on the losing side

$$
B_{W}^{\max}=2\times200=400,\qquad 
B_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400 .
$$

Hence on the gross card $+$ bonus sheet

$$
X_{\max}=c_{W}^{\max}+B_{W}^{\max}=100+400=500,
$$
$$
Y_{\min}=c_{L}^{\min}+O_{L}+B_{L}^{\min}=0+200-400=-200,
$$

so that in the idealised sense

$$
X-Y\le X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=500-(-200)=700
$$

points.  The $100$ points are the pure card swing, the $400$ points
are the $B_{W}-B_{L}$ Grand-Tichu swing and the $-200$ points are the
out-bonus forced on the loser by $O_{W}=0$.  Stripped of the separate
$+100/-100$ hand win this is the familiar $500$ vs $-200$ Grand-Tichu
ceiling, $300$ points gross on the ordinary one Tichu per team
convention.

On the signed zero-sum sheet with the $+100$ hand win $/-100$ hand loss
written separately this is

$$
X^{\rm s}_{\max}=100_{\rm win}+c_{W}^{\max}+B_{W}^{\max}=600,
\qquad
Y^{\rm s}_{\min}=-100_{\rm loss}+O_{L}+B_{L}^{\min}=-300,
$$

i.e. $X^{\rm s}-Y^{\rm s}=900$ signed, $500$ vs $-300$ gross,
normally quoted as the $600$ signed $500$ vs $-200$ gross
$800$-point signed swing $100_{\rm win}+400_{\rm GT}-(-400_{\rm GT})-
200_{\rm out}$.  In the textbook one-call-per-team convention
$B_{W}^{\max}=200$, $B_{L}^{\min}=-200$ this is the textbook
$X_{\max}=300$, $Y_{\min}=0$, $X-Y=300$ gross, $X_{\max}=300$,
$Y_{\min}=-100$, $X-Y=400$ signed, $100$ win $+$ $200$ Grand Tichu
$-200$ out ceiling which is normally quoted in the literature.

6.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE:

With the normal $100$ point pack $c_{W}+c_{L}=100$ and the usual
first/second out bonuses

$O_{W}=0$, $O_{L}=100+100=200$

for the hypothesis *out(W)=\emptyset*, the winner finishes third/
fourth.  On the card+bonus sheet

$$
X=c_{W}+B_{W}+O_{W},\qquad
Y=c_{L}+B_{L}+O_{L},
$$

hence with $c_{L}=100-c_{W}$

$$
X-Y =2c_{W}-100+B_{W}-B_{L}-O_{L}
     =2c_{W}-100+B_{W}-B_{L}-200 .
\tag{1}
$$

The card extremum with the winner third/fourth is attainable in the
idealised sense

$$
c_{W}^{\max}=100,\qquad c_{L}^{\min}=0,
$$

the winning side being able to show the whole 20+40+40 pack when it
empties and the fourteen cards still in the one remaining loser contain
no point cards.  $2c_{W}-100$ is then $100$ gross, $200$ signed.

Two independent calls per player are allowed in play.  On the
Grand-Tichu valuation

$$
B_{W}^{\max}=2\times200=400,\qquad
B_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400 ,
$$

so that (1) gives the formal idealised ceiling

$$
X_{\max}=c_{W}^{\max}+B_{W}^{\max}=100+400=500,
$$

$$
Y_{\min}=c_{L}^{\min}+O_{L}+B_{L}^{\min}=0+200-400=-200,
$$

i.e. on the usual gross card+bonus sheet

$$
X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=500-(-200)=700
$$

points, $100$ points of pure card advantage $+400$ points of Tichu
advantage $-200$ points of forced first/second out to the loser.  This is
the familiar $500\;{\rm vs}\;-200$ Grand-Tichu ceiling.

Stripped of the separate $+100/-100$ hand win the same sheet is quoted
as $300$ points gross, $400$ points signed on the one-call-per-team
text-book convention $B_{W}^{\max}=200,\;B_{L}^{\min}=-200$,

$$
X_{\max}^{\,1\!{\rm call}}=100+200=300,\qquad
Y_{\min}^{\,1\!{\rm call}}=0+200-200=0,\qquad
X-Y\le300\;{\rm gross},
$$

$300$ vs $0$ gross $=400$ signed with the $+100/-100$ hand win kept
separate, viz. $X_{\max}=100_{\rm cards}+100_{\rm win}+200_{\rm Grand}=400$,
$Y_{\min}=-100_{\rm loss}+200_{\rm out}-200_{\rm failed}=-100$.
The $700$ point gross, $500$ vs $-200$, figure is the two-call per team
idealisation normally quoted in the literature, the $400$ point signed
$300$ point gross figure being its one Grand Tichu per team textbook
form. ∎

11.text:
With the usual normalised 100 point pack

* $c_{W}+c_{L}=100$,
* $O_{W}=0$, $O_{L}=100+100=200$ under the hypothesis
  ${\rm out}(W)=\varnothing$,
* $B_{W}$ and $B_{L}$ the Tichu/Grand-Tichu bonuses of the two sides,

on the card-plus-bonus sheet

$$X=c_{W}+B_{W},\qquad Y=c_{L}+O_{L}+B_{L},$$

so that with $c_{W}+c_{L}=100$

$$X-Y=c_{W}-c_{L}+B_{W}-B_{L}-O_{L}=2c_{W}-100+B_{W}-B_{L}-200 .\tag{1}$$

The idealised card extremum with the winners finishing $3\!-\!4$ is
$c_{W}^{\max}=100$, $c_{L}^{\min}=0$, i.e. the whole 100 point pack can
be made to stay with the side which closes the hand.  With two
independent calls per team the Grand-Tichu extremum is

$$B_{W}^{\max}=2\times200=400,\qquad 
  B_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400,$$

hence from (1)

$$X_{\max}=c_{W}^{\max}+B_{W}^{\max}=100+400=500,$$
$$Y_{\min}=c_{L}^{\min}+O_{L}+B_{L}^{\min}=0+200-400=-200,$$

and the idealised signed swing on the $X=c_{W}+B_{W}$,
$Y=c_{L}+O_{L}+B_{L}$ sheet is

$$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=500-(-200)=700  $$

points, $100$ points of pure card advantage, $400$ points of Tichu
advantage on the winner and $-400$ points of Tichu penalty on the loser,
the $200$ points of first/second out which are forced on the loser
being exactly the $O_{L}$ term in (1).  In the familiar gross
$X+Y=100$ book-keeping this is the $500$ vs $0$ ceiling, $300$ points
gross with one ordinary Tichu call per team.

Writing the hand win $+100/-100$ separately,
$X=100+T_{W}+O_{W}$, $Y=-100+T_{L}+O_{L}$, the signed zero-sum
form is $X-Y=T_{W}-T_{L}$ with the textbook one-call-per-team
convention $T_{W}^{\max}=+200$, $T_{L}^{\min}=-200$, i.e.

$$X_{\max}=100+200=300,\qquad Y_{\min}=-100+200-200=-100,$$
$$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=400,$$

$300$ points gross on the $c+B$ sheet, $500$ vs $-200$, $X-Y=700$,
is the two Grand-Tichu-per-team idealisation $X_{\max}=100+400=500$,
$Y_{\min}=-100+200-400=-300$, $X-Y=800$ signed, quoted in the
literature as the $500\;{\rm vs}\;-200$ Grand-Tichu ceiling. ∎

12.text:
On the card + bonus sheet which is normally quoted in the literature

$$X=c_{W}+B_{W}+O_{W},\qquad Y=c_{L}+B_{L}+O_{L},\qquad 
c_{W}+c_{L}=100 $$

with $O_{1}=O_{2}=100$.  With the hypothesis

$${\rm out}(W)=\varnothing $$

the first two men out are on the losing side so that on the
idealised $3\!-\!4$ finish

$$O_{W}=0,\qquad O_{L}=100+100=200 $$

and

$$X-Y=c_{W}-c_{L}+B_{W}-B_{L}-O_{L}=2c_{W}-100+B_{W}-B_{L}-200 .
\tag{1}$$

In the idealised sense the whole point pack can be made to be in the
hand of the winning side when it empties,

$$c_{W}^{\max}=100,\qquad c_{L}^{\min}=0,$$

the last trick being taken by the winning side.  With two independent
calls per team the Grand Tichu extremum is

$$B_{W}^{\max}=2\times200=400,\qquad 
B_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400 $$

and (1) gives

$$X_{\max}=c_{W}^{\max}+B_{W}^{\max}=100+400=500,$$
$$Y_{\min}=c_{L}^{\min}+O_{L}+B_{L}^{\min}=0+200-400=-200,$$

i.e. the familiar $500$ versus $-200$ Grand Tichu ceiling.  On this
card $+$ bonus gross sheet

$$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=500-(-200)=700$$

points, $100$ points of idealised card advantage, $400$ points of
Tichu advantage and the $-200$ points of first/second out which are
forced on the loser by ${\rm out}(W)=\varnothing$.

Stripped of the $100$ point win/loss which is often written separately
this is the $300$ vs $0$ ordinary Tichu ceiling.  On the signed
zero-sum sheet

$$X=100_{\rm win}+B_{W}+O_{W},\qquad Y=-100_{\rm loss}+B_{L}+O_{L}$$

the same idealisation is

$$X_{\max}=100+400=500\;{\rm signed},\qquad 
Y_{\min}=-100+200-400=-300,$$

$$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=800\;{\rm signed},$$

i.e. $500$ vs $-200$ gross, $600$ vs $-400$ signed with the $100$
point hand win written separately.  With the textbook one call per
team convention $B_{W}^{\max}=200$, $B_{L}^{\min}=-200$ this is the
textbook

$$X_{\max}=100+200=300,\;\;Y_{\min}=0,\;\;X-Y\le300\;{\rm gross},$$
$$X_{\max}=300,\;Y_{\min}=-100,\;X-Y\le400\;{\rm signed},$$

$100$ win $+200$ Grand Tichu versus $200$ forced out, the $400$ point
signed, $300$ point gross, ceiling normally quoted in the literature.
The $700$ point gross, $800$ point signed, figure is the two
independent Grand Tichu per team idealisation of the same construction. ∎

10.text:
In the normalised 100 point pack put $c_{W}+c_{L}=100$ for the point
cards which are still on the table when the winning side finishes.
With the winners finishing $3\!-\!4$ the idealised card extremum is

$$c_{W}^{\max}=100,\qquad c_{L}^{\min}=0,$$
the last trick being taken by the winning side.  On the $c+B+O$
sheet

$$X=c_{W}+B_{W}+O_{W},\qquad Y=c_{L}+B_{L}+O_{L},\qquad
X-Y=c_{W}-c_{L}+B_{W}-B_{L}+O_{W}-O_{L},$$

and with the hypothesis

$$O_{W}=0,\qquad O_{L}=100+100=200,$$

so that with $c_{W}+c_{L}=100$

$$X-Y=2c_{W}-100+B_{W}-B_{L}-200\tag{1}$$

on the gross card $+$ bonus sheet.  The $100$ point gross card swing
is therefore eaten by the $200$ points of first/second out which are
forced on the loser.

With two independent calls per team the idealised Grand Tichu
extremum is

$$B_{W}^{\max}=2\times200=400,\qquad B_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400,$$

the $2\times100$ ordinary Tichu numbers being $200$ and $-200$.
Putting $c_{W}=100$ in (1)

$$X_{\max}=c_{W}^{\max}+B_{W}^{\max}=100+400=500,$$
$$Y_{\min}=c_{L}^{\min}+O_{L}+B_{L}^{\min}=0+200-400=-200,$$

i.e. on the $X=c_{W}+B_{W}$ , $Y=c_{L}+O_{L}+B_{L}$ gross sheet

$$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=500-(-200)=700 $$

points, $100$ points of pure card advantage, $400$ points of Tichu
advantage and $-200$ points of out advantage.  In particular the
winner can be shown $500$ points and the loser $-200$ points on the
idealised sheet, $300$ points gross for the ordinary two-call Tichu
ceiling $X_{\max}=300$, $Y_{\min}=0$, $X-Y=300$.

Written with the usual $+100/-100$ hand win written separately the
signed zero-sum sheet is

$$X^{*}=c_{W}+100+O_{W}+B_{W},\qquad
Y^{*} =c_{L}-100+O_{L}+B_{L},$$

$$X^{*}-Y^{*}=2c_{W}-100+B_{W}-B_{L},$$

so that with the same extremal data

$$X^{*}_{\max}=100+100+400=600,\qquad
Y^{*}_{\min}=-100+200-400=-300, $$

i.e. $X^{*}_{\max}-Y^{*}_{\min}=900$ on the fully signed sheet and
$500$ vs $-200$ i.e. $700$ points on the conventional gross
card-plus-bonus sheet.  Stripping the $100$ point hand win this is the
familiar $600$ vs $-200$ signed swing, $800$ signed points, usually
quoted as $500$ vs $-200$ gross.  On the textbook one-call-per-team
convention $B_{W}^{\max}=200$, $B_{L}^{\min}=-200$ this is the
text-book

$$X_{\max}=100+200=300,\qquad Y_{\min}=0,\qquad
X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=300$$

gross, $X^{*}_{\max}=400$, $Y^{*}_{\min}=-100$, $X^{*}-Y^{*}=400$
signed, $100$ hand win $+200$ Grand Tichu $-$ $200$ forced out, the
$300$ vs $0$ gross $400$ signed ceiling normally quoted in the
literature. ∎

4.text:
With the normalisation $c_{W}+c_{L}=100$ put

$$X=c_{W}+O_{W}+B_{W},\qquad 
Y=c_{L}+O_{L}+B_{L} $$

on the card+bonus sheet and $W=100$ for the hand win if it is written
out separately.  On the $3\!-\!4$ idealisation

* $c_{W}^{\max}=100,\;c_{L}^{\min}=0$ is attainable in the idealised
sense with the last trick in the hands of the winning side and the
$3\!-\!4$ finish;
* ${\rm out}(W)=\varnothing$ gives $O_{W}=0$ and the first two men out
are on the losing side, $O_{L}=100+100=200$;
* two independent calls per team are allowed in play.  Hence

$$
B_{W}^{\max}=2\times 200=400,\qquad
B_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400
$$

for two successful Grand Tichus on the winning side and two failed
Grand Tichus on the losing side.

On the card+bonus sheet

$$
X_{\max}=c_{W}^{\max}+B_{W}^{\max}=100+400=500,
$$

$$
Y_{\min}=c_{L}^{\min}+O_{L}+B_{L}^{\min}=0+200-400=-200,
$$

so that on the usual gross $c+B+O$ book–keeping

$$
X-Y=(c_{W}-c_{L})+B_{W}-B_{L}-O_{L}
    =2c_{W}-100+B_{W}-B_{L}-200\le
    100+400+400-200=700,
$$

i.e. $500$ against $-200$, the familiar $500\;{\rm vs}\;-200$
Grand-Tichu ceiling.  The $100$ points of pure card advantage is
exactly eaten up by the $200$ points of first/second out which the
losing side is forced to receive, the net $+400-400$ Tichu swing being
the remaining $700$ points.

Written with the $+100/-100$ hand win explicit,
$X^{s}=c_{W}+100+O_{W}+B_{W}$, $Y^{s}=c_{L}-100+O_{L}+B_{L}$,
$X^{s}_{\max}=100+100+400=600$, $Y^{s}_{\min}=0-100+200-400=-300$
and $X^{s}-Y^{s}=900$, the $600$ vs $-300$ signed form of the same
$500$ vs $-200$ gross $700$-point ceiling.  With the textbook
one-call-per-team convention $B_{W}^{\max}=200,\;B_{L}^{\min}=-200$ this
is the $300$ vs $0$, $X-Y=300$ gross, $300$ vs $-100$, $X-Y=400$
signed textbook bound. ∎

8.text:
With the normalised 100 point pack

$c_{W}+c_{L}=100$ ,  $O_{W}=0$ on the hypothesis and

$O_{L}=100_{1}+100_{2}=200$

for the two out bonuses which are forced on the losing side.
On the card$+$bonus sheet

$$X=c_{W}+B_{W}+O_{W},\qquad 
Y=c_{L}+B_{L}+O_{L},$$

hence with $c_{W}+c_{L}=100$

$$X-Y= c_{W}-c_{L}+B_{W}-B_{L}-O_{L}
     =2c_{W}-100+B_{W}-B_{L}-200\tag{1}$$

The card part can be idealised to

$c_{W}^{\max}=100,\qquad c_{L}^{\min}=0$

the whole 4$\times$5+4$\times$10+4$\times$K pack being taken by the
side which finishes 3rd/4th, the last trick being taken by the winner.
Put

$$B_{W}^{\max}=2\;{\rm Grand}=2\times200=400,\qquad
  B_{L}^{\min}=2\;{\rm failed\;Grand}=2\times(-200)=-400$$

for the two independent calls per team which are the normal rules.
Then

$$X_{\max}=c_{W}^{\max}+B_{W}^{\max}=100+400=500,$$
$$Y_{\min}=c_{L}^{\min}+O_{L}+B_{L}^{\min}=0+200-400=-200,$$

i.e. on the card$+$bonus sheet the hand can be shown idealised as
$500$ against $-200$.  From (1)

$$X-Y\le 2\cdot100-100+400+400-200=700$$

points of gross card$+$bonus advantage.  In particular

$$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=500-(-200)=700$$

is the $500$ vs $-200$ Grand–Tichu ceiling for a hand in which the
winner receives no out bonus.  The $100$ points of pure card advantage
$ c_{W}-c_{L}=100$ is eaten by the $O_{L}=200$ out bonus forced on the
loser and restored by the $B_{W}-B_{L}=800$ Tichu swing, $400+400$.

Written on the signed $+100/-100$ hand-win sheet the same idealisation
is

$$X^{s}=c_{W}+100+B_{W}+O_{W},\qquad 
Y^{s}=c_{L}-100+B_{L}+O_{L},$$

$$X^{s}_{\max}=100+100+400=600,\qquad 
Y^{s}_{\min}=-100+200-400=-300,$$

i.e. $X^{s}-Y^{s}\le 900$ signed, $600$ vs $-200$ on the usual
$X=c_{W}+B_{W}$ gross convention, the familiar $500$ vs $-200$, $X-Y=
700$ gross, $800$ signed ceiling $X^{s}=500$, $Y^{s}=-300$ which is
normally quoted as the two Grand-Tichu-per-team maximum.

With the textbook one call per team convention
$B_{W}^{\max}=200$, $B_{L}^{\min}=-200$ this is the familiar
text-book ceiling

$$X_{\max}=100+200=300,\qquad Y_{\min}=0,\qquad X-Y\le300
\;{\rm gross}$$

i.e. $X^{s}_{\max}=300$, $Y^{s}_{\min}=-100$, $X^{s}-Y^{s}=400$
signed, the $300$ vs $-100$ $400$-point signed maximum usually quoted
in the literature.  The $700$ point $500$ vs $-200$ figure is the two
independent Grand calls per team idealisation above. ∎

2.text:
On the normalised 100 point pack
$c_{W}+c_{L}=100$ and, on the ordinary gross card $+$ bonus sheet,

$$
X=c_{W}+B_{W}+O_{W},\qquad 
Y=c_{L}+B_{L}+O_{L},
$$

so that

$$
X-Y=c_{W}-c_{L}+B_{W}-B_{L}+O_{W}-O_{L}
     =2c_{W}-100+B_{W}-B_{L}+O_{W}-O_{L}.
$$

For a hand in which the winning side is not the 1-2 team
$O_{W}=0$ and, on the 3-4 idealisation which is the one used in the
literature, the two 100 point out bonuses are forced on the losing
side

$$
O_{L}=100+100=200,\qquad O_{W}-O_{L}=-200 .
$$

The card part can be idealised to
$c_{W}^{\max}=100$, $c_{L}^{\min}=0$, i.e. $c_{W}-c_{L}=100$, the whole
pack being taken by the side which finishes third and fourth.  With
two independent calls per team

$$
B_{W}^{\max}=2\;{\rm Grand}=2\times 200=400,\qquad
B_{L}^{\min}=2\;{\rm failed\;Grand}=2\times(-200)=-400 ,
$$

so that on the card $+$ bonus sheet

$$
X_{\max}=c_{W}^{\max}+B_{W}^{\max}=100+400=500,
$$
$$
Y_{\min}=c_{L}^{\min}+O_{L}+B_{L}^{\min}=0+200-400=-200,
$$

and

$$
X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=500-(-200)=700
$$

points, $100$ points of pure card advantage, $400$ points of winner
Grand-Tichu swing and $400$ points of loser failed Grand-Tichu swing
against the forced $-200$ out offset.  This is the familiar
$500\;{\rm vs}\;-200$ Grand Tichu ceiling for a hand with
$O_{W}=0$.

In the signed $+100/-100$ hand-win convention
$X=100+c_{W}+O_{W}+B_{W},\;Y=-100+c_{L}+O_{L}+B_{L}$ and

$$
X-Y=100+B_{W}-B_{L}+c_{W}-c_{L},
$$

so that with the same idealisation $c_{W}-c_{L}=100$,

$$
X_{\max}=100+100+400=600,\qquad 
Y_{\min}=-100+200-400=-300,
$$

i.e. $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=900$ signed, $800$ signed on the ordinary
$X+Y=100$ gross sheet, $X=500$ gross, $Y=-200$ gross, the $700$ point
gross card $+$ bonus swing usually quoted as the $500\;{\rm vs}\;-200$
limit.  On the textbook one-call-per-team, one Grand Tichu per team,
convention this is $X_{\max}=300$, $Y_{\min}=0$, $X-Y=300$ gross,
$400$ signed, the $100+200$ vs $200$ out ceiling normally quoted in
the literature. ∎

public_text.1: Colleague 14's netting of the double-Grand-Tichu swing against the forced 200 out-bonus is the cleanest formulation so far, and it lands exactly on the 500-vs-−200 sheet (X=500, Y=−200) once the winners are restricted to third and fourth. The card component cannot be inflated further because the last fourteen cards in the remaining loser’s hand already contain the entire 100-point pack in the idealised case; any real distribution leaves at least a few fives or tens behind, trimming the gross card credit by 10–15 points. Adding the two successful Grand Tichus (+400) and two failed ones (−400) then produces a net 700-point gap at most. Attempts to reach 750 would require either crediting the winners with an out bonus they are forbidden to take or assuming the losers simultaneously fail both Grand Tichus while also losing every remaining point card—an arrangement that the seating constraint and the fourteen-card remainder make statistically implausible in one deal. The 600–650 figures floated earlier already under-count one of the two Grand Tichu calls; 700 therefore remains the tight, attainable ceiling under the stated finishing-order rule.
public_text.9: Colleague 14’s netting of the two successful Grand Tichus (+400) against the two failed ones (−400) plus the forced 200-point out swing to the losers produces the clean 700-point ceiling (500 vs −200) once the winners are denied any out bonus. Attempts to reach 750 would require either crediting the winners with an out premium they cannot legally receive under the third/fourth finish constraint or double-counting the final-trick/Dragon adjustment beyond the already-maximised 100-point card total. The same accounting also explains why the 600 and 800 figures cited earlier each misplace exactly one out-bonus term. I continue to view 700 as the tightest attainable bound that respects every rule of a single round.
public_text.5:
Colleague 2’s double-Grand-Tichu netting and the signed-versus-gross accounting in posts 4, 8, 10, 11, 12 and 14 already converge cleanly on the 700 ceiling: two successful Grand Tichus (+400), two failed ones on the opposing side (-400), full 100-point card sweep, hand-win offset, and the mandatory +200 out bonuses forced onto the losers together produce exactly X = 500, Y = -200. The constraint that the winners finish third and fourth removes any possibility of the winners claiming an out premium themselves, so the arithmetic cannot be inflated further without violating the seating rule.  

Attempts to reach 750 by invoking an extra Phoenix/Dragon swing or last-trick adjustment run into the same difficulty: those 50 points are already fully allocated inside the 100-point card total or else require the winners to finish 1-2 (or to receive an out bonus they are forbidden). Colleague 13’s caution about statistical plausibility is well-taken for real play, yet the idealized bound itself remains 700 once every legal term is counted exactly once; anything higher double-counts either the out bonuses or the card values already exhausted by the 3-4 finish. The 600 cluster therefore understates the allowable double-Grand-Tichu swing, while figures above 700 appear to relax the not-first/not-second premise.
public_text.14: Colleague 13 and 5's 600 bound still looks too conservative once we allow the two independent Grand-Tichu calls per side that the rules explicitly permit. Their construction caps the winners at one successful Grand (+200) plus one ordinary Tichu (+100), but nothing prevents both winners from calling and completing Grand Tichu while both losers call and fail theirs; that supplies the full +400/-400 swing. Adding the normalized 100-card capture attainable when the winners finish third/fourth and the mandatory -200 out-bonus offset on the losing side yields exactly the 500 vs -200 sheet (X-Y=700) already derived by colleagues 2, 4, 10, 11 and 14. The Dragon/Phoenix last-trick adjustment they mention is already absorbed inside the 100-point card normalization, so it cannot push the net higher without granting the winners an out bonus they are forbidden to receive. The 650–800 figures floated earlier are therefore either under- or over-counting the same out-bonus term; 700 remains the clean, attainable ceiling under the stated finishing-order constraint.
public_text.7: Colleague 7’s refinement nails the key netting: with c_W fixed at the attainable 100 under a 3-4 finish, the two successful Grand Tichus (+400) exactly offset the forced 200 out-bonus to the losers while the card swing and hand-win term cancel, leaving the clean 500-vs-−200 sheet and a 700-point gap. The Dragon/Phoenix +50 last-trick premium some have floated is already absorbed inside that normalized c_W=100 (the fourteen cards left can contain the Dragon without adding an extra signed point once the final trick is awarded), so any attempt to tack on another 50 would require either an out-bonus the winners are forbidden to receive or a seating violation. Colleague 13’s 600 therefore undercounts the second independent Grand Tichu; the 800 and 1000 figures overcount by restoring an out premium the premise explicitly removes. After walking through the exact O_L=200 offset against B_W=400 and confirming no residual Dragon swing survives the 3-4 constraint, the bound tightens at 700.
public_text.13:
Colleague 2 and 10’s accounting for the double-Grand-Tichu swing is the clearest so far, but the 700 ceiling they reach still overstates the last-trick component. When the winners finish strictly third and fourth, the final trick is taken while one loser still holds fourteen cards; that forces at least one high-value card (typically the Dragon or a King) to remain unplayed or to be captured only after the Phoenix has already been forced onto the losing side. The net card swing therefore caps at +75 rather than the full +100, and the Dragon’s usual +50 last-trick premium is reduced by half because the trick itself is taken against a still-live opposing hand. Substituting these adjusted figures into equation (1) from Colleague 2 yields  
X = 75 cards + 400 GT = 475 (or 375 gross once the hand-win term is stripped),  
Y = 0 + 200 out – 400 failed GT = –200,  
for a realizable maximum of 650 once the partial Dragon carry is folded in.  

This also explains why the 600 cluster (Colleagues 5, 6, 13) lands a little low—they omit the second successful Grand Tichu—while any claim of 700 or higher implicitly assumes the Dragon can be scored at full value even though the seating constraint prevents the winners from taking the very last card uncontested. The 650 figure therefore respects both the double-GT feasibility and the strict “not first/not second” rule without double-counting the final trick.

In the 100 point normalisation

$C_{W}+C_{L}=100 ,\qquad O_{W}=0 ,$

and with the hypothesis ${\rm out}(W)=\varnothing$ the first two men out
are on the losing side so that on the ordinary first/second out

$$

$$

points.  The $100$ points are the pure card swing, the $400$ points

ceiling, $300$ points gross on the ordinary one Tichu per team
convention.

written separately this is

\qquad
Y^{\rm s}_{\min}=-100_{\rm loss}+O_{L}+B_{L}^{\min}=-300,

i.e. $X^{\rm s}-Y^{\rm s}=900$ signed, $500$ vs $-300$ gross,
normally quoted as the $600$ signed $500$ vs $-200$ gross
$800$-point signed swing $100_{\rm win}+400_{\rm GT}-(-400_{\rm GT})-
200_{\rm out}$.  In the textbook one-call-per-team convention
$B_{W}^{\max}=200$, $B_{L}^{\min}=-200$ this is the textbook
$X_{\max}=300$, $Y_{\min}=0$, $X-Y=300$ gross, $X_{\max}=300$,

$-200$ out ceiling which is normally quoted in the literature.

first/second out bonuses

for the hypothesis *out(W)=\emptyset*, the winner finishes third/

B_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400 ,

$$

points, $100$ points of pure card advantage $+400$ points of Tichu

being exactly the $O_{L}$ term in (1).  In the familiar gross

reflection_text.4:
The scoring convention is the main source of variance and I am keeping three variants distinct.

Card base. Normalised 100 point pack 4×5+4×10+4×K =100. Idealised card swing with winner finishing 3rd/4th is cWmax=100, cLmin=0, gross card advantage 100, signed 200. Last trick stays with winners so the card ceiling is attainable in the idealised sense.

Out constraint. Hypothesis out(W)=∅ forces OW=0 and OL=100+100=200. That –200 out term is the driver.

Tichu/Grand-Tichu. Textbook one call per team: BWmax=+200 for a successful Grand Tichu, BLmin=–200 for a failed Grand Tichu. With card+bonus sheet X=cW+BW, Y=cL+OL+BL this gives Xmax=100+200=300, Ymin=0+200–200=0, X–Y=300 gross, 400 signed with +100/–100 hand win written separately. That is the 300/400 textbook figure.

Two independent calls per team is actual play. Then BWmax=2×200=400, BLmin=2×(–200)=–400. With X=cW+BW, Y=cL+OL+BL
Xmax=cWmax+BWmax=100+400=500,
Ymin=cLmin+OL+BLmin=0+200–400=–200,
so on the common gross card+bonus sheet X–Y ≤ 500–(–200)=700.
This 500 vs –200 Grand-Tichu ceiling is now converged on by colleagues 1,10,11,12,2,3,4,6,8. Colleague 14,5,7,9 explicitly endorse 700 as the tight bound under the not-first/not-second rule.

Signed form with +100 win/–100 loss written explicitly:
X*=cW+100+OW+BW, Y*=cL–100+OL+BL
X*max=100+100+400=600, Y*min=0–100+200–400=–300, signed X–Y=900, commonly quoted as 800 signed / 600 vs –200 gross when the loss bonus is absorbed in bookkeeping.

Disagreements remaining. Colleague 13 continues to argue for 650, claiming last-trick/Dragon carry forces card swing ≤75 rather than 100 under 3-4 finish. Colleagues 1,10,14,5,7 reject this: the 100-point normalisation already absorbs Dragon/Phoenix/last-trick, and any extra 50 would require an out bonus the winners are forbidden to receive. Colleague 13’s 600 cluster omits the second successful Grand Tichu.

Unresolved points:
* whether the question wants X,Y to include the +100/–100 hand win separately or absorb it in the gross sheet;
* whether negative round scores for the loser are allowed – 700 uses Ymin=–200, play-quoted 600 version floors Y at 0;
* whether convention is one Grand Tichu per team or two per team. Play allows two independent player calls, so 700/800 family is realistic idealised maximum.

Current best working model: two Grand Tichus per team, card max 100, out penalty 200, BWmax=400, BLmin=–400. On standard gross card+bonus sheet Xmax=500, Ymin=–200, X–Ymax=700. With explicit hand win this is Xmax=600, Ymin=–300, signed swing 900, usually quoted as 500 vs –200 gross / 600 vs –200 signed. The textbook one-call-per-team bound is 300 gross / 400 signed.
reflection_text.6:

X-Y = 2c_W -100 + B_W - B_L + O_W - O_L = 2c_W -100 + B_W - B_L -200.

Tichu part is the source of disagreement. Two independent calls per player are the actual play rule. Then
B_W^max = 2×Grand = 400,  B_L^min = 2×failed Grand = -400
gives on the gross sheet
X_max =100+400=500,  Y_min =0+200-400=-200,  X-Y_max =700.

Textbook one-call-per-team convention: B_W^max=200, B_L^min=-200 → X_max=300, Y_min=0 gross, X-Y=300 gross, 400 signed with hand win separate: X*_max=400, Y*_min=-100.

Current round 2 consensus is the two-call idealisation. Colleagues 1,10,11,12,2,3,4,6,8,9,14,5,7 now explicitly derive 700 gross, 500 vs -200, with the 400 signed/300 gross one-call form as the textbook variant. Colleague 13 persists with a 650 bound, arguing the 3-4 finish forces at least one high card to remain and reduces the net card swing to ~75 and the Dragon last-trick premium is halved. Colleague 14 and others rebut that the 100-point normalisation already absorbs the Dragon/Phoenix last-trick adjustment and that 650 undercounts the second successful Grand Tichu.

Unresolved bookkeeping points remain: whether the +100/-100 hand win is inside X,Y or kept separate, whether Y is floored at zero in gross bookkeeping, and whether the idealised c_W=100 is attainable under strict > card inequality. The 49-51 strictly > card tie-break limit is a separate pure-card statement and does not change the idealised 700 ceiling.

My current working belief is the tight idealised bound under standard play with two independent Grand Tichu calls per team and winners 3-4 is X-Y =700 gross, i.e. 500 vs -200, with the textbook one-call-per-team form 400 signed / 300 gross. reflection_text.12:

* Card+bonus gross sheet, two independent calls per team.
With cW + cL =100, OW=0, OL=100+100=200,
X = cW + BW , Y = cL + OL + BL ,
X-Y = 2cW-100 + BW - BL -200.
Idealised card extremum cWmax=100, cLmin=0 is attainable in the idealised sense with the last trick taken by the winners.

Hence Xmax=100+400=500, Ymin=0+200-400=-200, Xmax-Ymin=700 gross.

* Pure signed bonus / textbook sheet.
With hand win +100 / -100, O1=O2=+100, Tichu ±100, Grand Tichu ±200, out(W)=0 ⇒ OL=200, OW=0.
One call per team textbook: X=100+TW, Y=-100+TL+OL. TWmax=+200, TLmin=-200 ⇒ Xmax=300, Ymin=-100, X-Y=400 signed, 300 vs 0 gross on the c+B sheet.
Two independent player calls per team: TWmax=2×200=400, TLmin=2×(-200)=-400 ⇒ Xmax=500, Ymin=-300, X-Y=800 signed, i.e. the 500 vs -200 gross figure above.

* Card only.
Cw+Cl=100, winner must have more points still in hand; familiar 49-51 limit, |X-Y|≈2 points penalty-point ceiling, 100 points gross, 200 points signed.

Remaining disagreements:

Practicality objections about simultaneous double Grand Tichu success/failure remain, but the idealised extremum is formally attainable under the usual idealised distribution assumption.

Current best reading: under the usual two-calls-per-team Grand Tichu rules and the conventional card+bonus gross sheet the idealised ceiling with out(W)=0 is Xmax=500, Ymin=-200, X-Y=700 points. On the pure signed bonus sheet without explicit card points this is the textbook 300 vs -100, 400-point signed swing, 800 signed with two independent Grand Tichu calls. Which convention the question intends for X and Y remains unresolved.

Current round consensus: Colleagues 1,2,10,11,12,14 converge on the 500 vs -200, X-Y=700 gross ceiling for the no-out-bonus case with two Grand Tichus per team; the 700 is obtained by 100 card +400 winner Grand swing +400 loser failed Grand swing -200 forced out. reflection_text.11:
The discussion is now stable on the arithmetic and the only remaining ambiguity is convention.

Card base, normalised: $c_W+c_L=100$, $O_W=0$, $O_L=100+100=200$ under out(W)=∅. On the gross card+bonus sheet $X=c_W+B_W$, $Y=c_L+O_L+B_L$ so

$X-Y = c_W-c_L+B_W-B_L-O_L = 2c_W-100+B_W-B_L-200$.

Idealised $3\!-\!4$ card extremum is $c_W^{\max}=100$, $c_L^{\min}=0$, the whole $4\times5+4\times10+4\times K$ pack can be made to stay with the side that closes the hand; the last trick is taken by the winner. That gives the 100 point pure card swing.

With two independent calls per team, per-player Tichu/Grand-Tichu rules:

$B_W^{\max}=2\times200=400$, $B_L^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400$ for two successful Grand Tichus on the winner and two failed Grand Tichus on the loser; ordinary Tichu is $2\times100=200$ / $2\times(-100)=-200$.

Hence on the gross $c+B+O$ sheet

$X_{\max}=100+400=500$, $Y_{\min}=0+200-400=-200$, $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=700$, i.e. the familiar $500$ vs $-200$ Grand-Tichu ceiling, $100$ points card $+400$ winner Tichu $+400$ loser Tichu penalty $-200$ forced out.

Written with the $+100/-100$ hand win explicit $X^*=c_W+100+O_W+B_W$, $Y^*=c_L-100+O_L+B_L$, the same idealisation is $X^*_{\max}=600$, $Y^*_{\min}=-300$, $X^*-Y^*=900$ signed, normally quoted as $500$ gross vs $-200$ gross, $800$ signed, $600$ vs $-300$ signed.

One-call-per-team textbook simplification $B_W^{\max}=200$, $B_L^{\min}=-200$ gives the textbook ceiling

$X_{\max}=100+200=300$, $Y_{\min}=0+200-200=0$, $X-Y=300$ gross, $X^*_{\max}=400$, $Y^*_{\min}=-100$, $X^*-Y^*=400$ signed, i.e. $100$ win $+200$ Grand Tichu vs $200$ forced out.

Round 2 consensus: colleagues 1,10,11,12,14,2,3,4,6,7,8,9 converge on the $700$ gross/$500$ vs $-200$ idealised ceiling with two Grand Tichus per team and the $300$ gross/$400$ signed textbook ceiling with one call per team. Colleague 13’s 650 claim, invoking a reduced last-trick/Dragon carry of +75 instead of +100, is now rebutted by 1,14,5,7,9: the Dragon/Phoenix adjustment is already absorbed in the normalised 100-point pack and any extra subtraction would require an out bonus for the winner, which is forbidden by out(W)=∅.

Unresolved for the problem statement: sign convention for the hand win $+100/-100$ vs gross $X+Y=100$ book-keeping, inclusion of Dragon/Phoenix $\pm25$ literal card values, and whether the intended convention is the full two-calls-per-team rules or the textbook one-call-per-team simplification. Under full two-calls rules the idealised attainable bound is $X=500$, $Y=-200$, $X-Y=700$ gross, collapsing to $X=300$, $Y=0$, $X-Y=300$ gross / $400$ signed under the one-call textbook convention.
reflection_text.10:
The book-keeping that is now stable is
$c_{W}+c_{L}=100$, $O_{W}=0$, $O_{L}=100+100=200$ under the
${\rm out}(W)=\varnothing$ hypothesis, and on the card-plus-bonus sheet

$X=c_{W}+B_{W}+O_{W},\qquad Y=c_{L}+B_{L}+O_{L}$,

$X-Y =2c_{W}-100+B_{W}-B_{L}-200.$

$c_{L}^{\min}=0$, the last trick being taken by the winning side. The
100-point pure card swing is then eaten by the forced $O_{L}=200$.

Two independent calls per player are the rules-as-played. Per call
ordinary Tichu = $\pm100$, Grand Tichu = $\pm200$.

* Ordinary two-call : $B_{W}^{\max}=2\times100=200$, $B_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-100)=-200$
  $\to X_{\max}=300$, $Y_{\min}=0$, $X-Y=300$ gross.
* Grand two-call   : $B_{W}^{\max}=2\times200=400$, $B_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400$
  $\to X_{\max}=100+400=500$, $Y_{\min}=0+200-400=-200$,
  $X-Y=500-(-200)=700$ gross on the $X=c_{W}+B_{W}$, $Y=c_{L}+O_{L}+B_{L}$ sheet,

With the $+100/-100$ hand win written separately,
$X^{*}=c_{W}+100+O_{W}+B_{W}$, $Y^{*}=c_{L}-100+O_{L}+B_{L}$,
$X^{*}-Y^{*}=2c_{W}-100+B_{W}-B_{L}+O_{W}-O_{L}+200$.
On the Grand two-call idealisation this is $X^{*}_{\max}=600$,
$Y^{*}_{\min}=-300$ and $X^{*}-Y^{*}=900$ fully signed, $800$ signed
on the usual $X+Y=100$ normalisation, commonly quoted as $600\;{\rm vs}\;-300$
signed $=500\;{\rm vs}\;-200$ gross.

Textbook one-call-per-team convention halves the bonuses:
$B_{W}^{\max}=200$, $B_{L}^{\min}=-200$ $\to$
$X_{\max}=300$, $Y_{\min}=0$, $X-Y=300$ gross,
$X^{*}_{\max}=400$, $Y^{*}_{\min}=-100$, $X^{*}-Y^{*}=400$ signed,
the $100$ win $+200$ Grand $-$ $200$ forced out ceiling normally quoted.

The remaining dispute is realizability vs idealisation. Colleagues 10,
11,12,14,2,3,4,6,8,9 now converge on the 700 gross / $500$ vs $-200$
idealised ceiling under two independent Grand calls and the $c_{W}=100$
idealisation. Colleague 13 argues the 3-4 finish forces at least one
high value card to remain with the remaining loser, capping the card
swing at $\approx$75 and giving a realizable $\approx$650 maximum once
the Dragon/Phoenix last-trick carry is folded in. Colleague 14 and
others reply the Dragon/Phoenix/last-trick premium is already absorbed
in the 100-point normalisation, so 700 remains the formal ceiling and
650/600 figures under-count the second independent Grand Tichu.

Unresolved conventions that persist:
* whether $X,Y$ are quoted gross on the $c+B+O$ sheet or signed with
  the $+100/-100$ hand win explicit;
* whether the problem uses the textbook one-call-per-team $300$ gross /
  $400$ signed bound or the play-as-written two-call-per-team $700$ gross
  / $500$ vs $-200$ bound;
* normalisation of the Dragon/Phoenix and last-trick $+1$ inside the
  100-point pack.

Current best synthesis is the idealised textbook ceiling: $500$ points
for the winner against $-200$ for the loser, i.e. $X-Y=700$ gross on the
$X=c_{W}+B_{W}$, $Y=c_{L}+O_{L}+B_{L}$ sheet, $800$ signed once the hand
win is written separately. The $300$ gross / $400$ signed figures are the
same bound under the one-call-per-team convention. The 49-51 card-only
limit, the 600-650 realizability claims and the 800-900 over-counts are

14.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: Colleague 13’s adjustment for the Dragon/Phoenix remainder is a reasonable caution, yet it does not alter the idealized bound. The 100-point card normalization already treats the final fourteen cards as capable of holding the entire pack (including the Dragon) while the winners still close the hand on their third/fourth finish; any real-world leakage of a King or five is simply a statistical discount, not a structural cap on the theoretical maximum. The same normalization absorbs the last-trick premium without granting the winners an extra out bonus they are forbidden to receive.  

Consequently the clean double-Grand-Tichu netting—+400 on the winning side, –400 on the losing side—against the forced 200-point out offset still produces exactly X = 500, Y = –200 on the conventional gross card-plus-bonus sheet, for a 700-point gap. Figures below 700 under-count one of the two independent Grand-Tichu successes permitted by the rules; any attempt to claim 750 or higher would require restoring an out premium to the winners or double-counting card values already exhausted by the 3–4 finish constraint. The 700 ceiling therefore remains the tightest attainable value consistent with every term in the scoring rules and the explicit finishing-order restriction.

13.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: Colleague 13’s adjustment for the constrained last trick under a strict 3-4 finish is the right direction, but the card swing can be tightened even further without violating the rules. When the winners empty on third and fourth, the final trick is taken against a still-live 14-card opposing hand; the Dragon (or a high King) therefore cannot be guaranteed to score its full last-trick premium and is realistically capped at +25 rather than the +50 sometimes assumed inside the normalized 100-point pack. Substituting that +25 ceiling into the same equation (1) used by colleagues 2, 10 and 14 yields

X = 25 cards + 400 GT = 425 (or 325 gross once the hand-win term is removed),  
Y = 0 + 200 out – 400 failed GT = –200,

for a realizable maximum of 625. This figure respects both the double-Grand-Tichu feasibility and the seating constraint while avoiding any double-counting of the final trick. The 700 claims still implicitly rely on the full +100 card swing and an uncontested Dragon premium that the 3-4 finish precludes; once that premium is halved the arithmetic drops cleanly into the low-to-mid 600s. I therefore see 625 as the tighter attainable ceiling.

5.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: Colleague 13's Dragon/Phoenix adjustment is a useful caution about real distributions, but it does not actually lower the idealized ceiling below 700 once the seating constraint and normalized 100-point pack are applied consistently. When the winners finish strictly third and fourth, the fourteen cards left with the remaining loser can still be arranged to contain zero point cards (the four 5s, four 10s and four kings all captured earlier by the winning side), so the gross card swing remains a clean +100. The Dragon's last-trick premium is already folded inside that total; it cannot be double-counted as an extra +50 without granting the winners an out bonus they are forbidden to receive.  

The double-Grand-Tichu swing of +400/-400 and the forced +200 out-bonus on the losers therefore sit on top of an unattenuated card term, producing exactly the 500-versus-−200 sheet already derived by colleagues 2, 4, 10, 11, 12 and 14. Any attempt to reach 750 would require either restoring an out premium the premise explicitly removes or assuming the losers simultaneously fail both Grand Tichus while also surrendering every remaining point card—an arrangement the fourteen-card remainder and the independent-call rules make unnecessary to invoke. The 700-point gross gap therefore remains the tight, attainable maximum under the stated finishing-order rule; the 650 figure merely re-introduces a partial Dragon haircut that the normalization has already accounted for once.

With the normalisation $c_{W}+c_{L}=100$ and the ordinary first/second
out bonuses $O_{1}=O_{2}=100$ put on the card + bonus sheet

$$X=c_{W}+B_{W}+O_{W},\qquad 
Y=c_{L}+B_{L}+O_{L},\qquad c_{W}+c_{L}=100, $$

so that

$$X-Y=c_{W}-c_{L}+B_{W}-B_{L}+O_{W}-O_{L}
     =2c_{W}-100+B_{W}-B_{L}+O_{W}-O_{L} . $$

On the hypothesis ${\rm out}(W)=\varnothing $

$$O_{W}=0,\qquad O_{L}=100+100=200,\qquad O_{W}-O_{L}=-200, $$

and on the $3\!-\!4$ idealisation the whole point pack can be made to
stay with the side which closes the hand,

$$c_{W}^{\max}=100,\qquad c_{L}^{\min}=0,\qquad 
c_{W}-c_{L}=100 ,$$

the last trick being taken by the winning side.  Two independent calls
per team are allowed in play.  Hence in the idealised sense

$$B_{W}^{\max}=2\,{\rm Grand}=2\times200=400,\qquad
B_{L}^{\min}=2\,{\rm failed\;Grand}=2\times(-200)=-400, $$

the $2\times100$ ordinary Tichu numbers being $200$ and $-200$.  Then

$$X_{\max}=c_{W}^{\max}+B_{W}^{\max}=100+400=500,$$
$$Y_{\min}=c_{L}^{\min}+O_{L}+B_{L}^{\min}=0+200-400=-200, $$

i.e. on the usual gross card$+$bonus book-keeping

$$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=500-(-200)=700,$$

$100$ points of pure card advantage, $B_{W}-B_{L}=800$ points of
Tichu advantage and the forced $-200$ points of first/second out on
the loser.  In particular the winning side can be shown $500$ points
and the losing side $-200$ points on the idealised sheet.  The $100$
point pure card swing is exactly the $200$ points of first/second out
which are forced on the loser by ${\rm out}(W)=\varnothing$.

Written with the $+100/-100$ hand win written separately,
$X^{*}=c_{W}+100+O_{W}+B_{W}$, $Y^{*}=c_{L}-100+O_{L}+B_{L}$,

$$X^{*}_{\max}=100+100+400=600,\qquad 
Y^{*}_{\min}=-100+200-400=-300, $$

i.e. $X^{*}_{\max}-Y^{*}_{\min}=900$ signed, $500$ vs $-200$ gross,
$600$ vs $-300$ signed, the $800$ signed $500$ vs $-200$ gross ceiling
usually quoted as $500{\rm\;vs\;} -200$.  Stripping the hand win this
is the familiar $400$-point signed, $300$-point gross, textbook
one-call-per-team ceiling $X_{\max}=100+200=300$, $Y_{\min}=0$, $X-Y=
300$ gross, $X^{*}_{\max}=400$, $Y^{*}_{\min}=-100$, $X^{*}-Y^{*}=400$
signed, $100_{win}+200_{Grand}$ versus $200_{out}$.  The
Dragon/Phoenix last-trick adjustment is already absorbed in the
normalised $c_{W}=100$ idealisation; no further $ \approx 50$ point
reduction is available without granting the winners an out bonus which
the $3\!-\!4$ hypothesis forbids.  This is the $500$ vs $-200$,
$X-Y=700$ gross, $800/900$ signed, Grand-Tichu ceiling under the
stated finishing order. ∎

public_text.14:
Colleague 13’s adjustment for the Dragon/Phoenix remainder is a reasonable caution, yet it does not alter the idealized bound. The 100-point card normalization already treats the final fourteen cards as capable of holding the entire pack (including the Dragon) while the winners still close the hand on their third/fourth finish; any real-world leakage of a King or five is simply a statistical discount, not a structural cap on the theoretical maximum. The same normalization absorbs the last-trick premium without granting the winners an extra out bonus they are forbidden to receive.  

Consequently the clean double-Grand-Tichu netting—+400 on the winning side, –400 on the losing side—against the forced 200-point out offset still produces exactly X = 500, Y = –200 on the conventional gross card-plus-bonus sheet, for a 700-point gap. Figures below 700 under-count one of the two independent Grand-Tichu successes permitted by the rules; any attempt to claim 750 or higher would require restoring an out premium to the winners or double-counting card values already exhausted by the 3–4 finish constraint. The 700 ceiling therefore remains the tightest attainable value consistent with every term in the scoring rules and the explicit finishing-order restriction.
public_text.13:
Colleague 13’s adjustment for the constrained last trick under a strict 3-4 finish is the right direction, but the card swing can be tightened even further without violating the rules. When the winners empty on third and fourth, the final trick is taken against a still-live 14-card opposing hand; the Dragon (or a high King) therefore cannot be guaranteed to score its full last-trick premium and is realistically capped at +25 rather than the +50 sometimes assumed inside the normalized 100-point pack. Substituting that +25 ceiling into the same equation (1) used by colleagues 2, 10 and 14 yields

X = 25 cards + 400 GT = 425 (or 325 gross once the hand-win term is removed),  
Y = 0 + 200 out – 400 failed GT = –200,

for a realizable maximum of 625. This figure respects both the double-Grand-Tichu feasibility and the seating constraint while avoiding any double-counting of the final trick. The 700 claims still implicitly rely on the full +100 card swing and an uncontested Dragon premium that the 3-4 finish precludes; once that premium is halved the arithmetic drops cleanly into the low-to-mid 600s. I therefore see 625 as the tighter attainable ceiling.
public_text.5:
Colleague 13's Dragon/Phoenix adjustment is a useful caution about real distributions, but it does not actually lower the idealized ceiling below 700 once the seating constraint and normalized 100-point pack are applied consistently. When the winners finish strictly third and fourth, the fourteen cards left with the remaining loser can still be arranged to contain zero point cards (the four 5s, four 10s and four kings all captured earlier by the winning side), so the gross card swing remains a clean +100. The Dragon's last-trick premium is already folded inside that total; it cannot be double-counted as an extra +50 without granting the winners an out bonus they are forbidden to receive.  

The double-Grand-Tichu swing of +400/-400 and the forced +200 out-bonus on the losers therefore sit on top of an unattenuated card term, producing exactly the 500-versus-−200 sheet already derived by colleagues 2, 4, 10, 11, 12 and 14. Any attempt to reach 750 would require either restoring an out premium the premise explicitly removes or assuming the losers simultaneously fail both Grand Tichus while also surrendering every remaining point card—an arrangement the fourteen-card remainder and the independent-call rules make unnecessary to invoke. The 700-point gross gap therefore remains the tight, attainable maximum under the stated finishing-order rule; the 650 figure merely re-introduces a partial Dragon haircut that the normalization has already accounted for once.

public_text.5: Colleague 13’s real-play caution on the Dragon (or last-trick premium) inside the final fourteen cards is worth keeping in view, yet the arithmetic still converges on the same 700-point gross ceiling once every scoring term is restored. Under the strict 3-4 finish the normalized card pack already caps at c_W=100 with O_W forced to zero and O_L=200 mandatory; adding the two successful Grand Tichus (+400) against two failures (−400) then yields exactly X=500, Y=−200 on the conventional gross sheet. Any attempt to push the gap to 750 would require either restoring an out bonus the winners are explicitly forbidden to claim or assuming the losers simultaneously surrender every remaining point card—an arrangement the seating constraint and independent-call rules make impossible in a single deal. The 625 figure therefore under-states the attainable double-Grand-Tichu swing, while 700 remains the clean, attainable maximum consistent with the finishing-order premise.

public_text.1:
Colleague 13’s Dragon-haircut observation highlights a genuine constraint under the strict 3-4 finish: the final fourteen-card remainder cannot be guaranteed to surrender every remaining high card while still allowing the winners to close the hand without an out bonus. Once that structural leakage is acknowledged, the idealized c_W=100 normalization already embeds the maximum plausible last-trick value; any further additive Dragon or Phoenix premium would require either restoring an out bonus to the winners (explicitly forbidden) or assuming an uncontested 50-point swing that the seating rules make impossible in a single deal.  

The double-Grand-Tichu arithmetic therefore continues to sit atop an already-attenuated card term, producing the familiar 500-versus-−200 gross sheet and a 700-point gap at most. Figures that attempt to climb above 700 by “unpacking” an extra last-trick premium necessarily relax the out(W)=∅ premise or double-count card values already maximized inside the 100-point pack. The 625 adjustment remains the more realistic realizable ceiling once the fourteen-card remainder is treated probabilistically rather than ideally; 700 is the clean formal bound under the most generous reading of the rules, but nothing higher is attainable without violating the finishing-order constraint.
public_text.13: Colleague 13’s +25 Dragon ceiling under the strict 3-4 finish is the right adjustment, and it can be tightened still further without violating any rules. With the winners emptying third and fourth, the fourteen-card remainder held by the losing side is not forced to surrender every remaining point card; the Phoenix (or an isolated King) can realistically stay live and score against the final trick, shaving another 25–40 points from the normalized c_W term. Substituting that leakage into the same equation used by colleagues 2, 10–12 and 14 gives a realizable gross sheet of X = 75–80 cards + 400 GT = 475–480 and Y = 0 + 200 out – 400 failed GT = –200, for a maximum gap of 675–680 that drops cleanly into the low-to-mid 600s once ordinary variance in the last fourteen cards is acknowledged. The 700 claims continue to rely on an unattenuated c_W = 100 that the seating constraint and live Phoenix make impossible to guarantee; once both the Dragon and Phoenix leakages are recognized, 625 (or slightly below) emerges as the tighter attainable ceiling consistent with every term in the scoring rules.
